The next session reads the ADR and registers it once more. **When a decision moves, write every surface that described that decision in the same commit** (a recurrence of the S18.24 lesson "if it is nailed only in the ADR, it leaks" — this time in the opposite direction).
- **Review round 2 (a `SendMessage` delta to the same reviewer — not newly spawned): verdict FIX, all applied.** The reviewer confirmed by independent re-measurement that the 3 BLOCKs were closed. The remaining remarks were all of the type **"what was fixed is narrower than the claim of its own text"**: ① the new regex is **line-based so it cannot bite a group import that rustfmt split** (`use crate::{`⏎`  connection_core::A,`) — this repo has no `rustfmt.toml` and `cargo fmt --check` is a standing gate, so that form can be forcibly produced (confirmed the miss by synthetic reproduction → resolved with `-U`) ② **the positive control cannot catch a failure of the `super::` branch** — the 7 current real edges are all in the `crate::` form, so the control passes even if the prefix is narrowed again (stated explicitly not to approve a narrowing revision on the strength of the control) ③ **the second command of the same section and the condition 3 description were not fixed, leaving an asymmetry** (reproducing the same defect five lines below the warning — replaced together) ④ qa.md claimed "③ is unregistered" itself so **the status canonical source became two again** (→ pointer to the "registration state" line of ADR-0130 §Impact). `super(::super)?` also has a 2-level cap so it was replaced with `(super::)+`.
- **★2 S18.22 carried-over issues closed (user delegation — 「코드 수정 아니면 알아서」)★ — both were not "should we delete it" but "it closes if the role is declared":**
  - **① Isolation gate commands duplicated across 3 documents → keep + state the role line.** On measurement, **all three copies already carried a pointer to the canonical source (net `lib.rs` header)**, so expected-value rot was already blocked — the only remaining risk was the *command text* diverging. So I pinned the role per reader: `docs/testing-strategy.md` = **strategy narrative** (why this gate) · `/qa` binding = **execution copy** · CLAUDE.md 「빌드·검증 명령」 = **entry excerpt** (carries only gates 1~3 and declares itself an "excerpt" — **not canonical**) · net `lib.rs` header = **the canonical source of command text · expected values · rationale** (the only place holding all five gates). Deleting would leave two of the three readers (strategy understanding / execution / entry) lost. ★The draft designated CLAUDE.md as the canonical source of command text and **was BLOCKed in review round 4** — since it declares itself an excerpt and has no commands for gates 4 · 5 at all, sending sessions there would make them copy-paste the self-hit trap pattern into a fourth file.★
  - **② `architecture-overview.md` net paragraph → keep.** On reading the real text, that paragraph does not list figures and only points to the canonical source (the net crate header) — deleting it only removes the bird's-eye view and the rot stays. (What was touched in S18.25 ④ was one duplicated figure in the *daemon* paragraph, a different matter.)
  - **The command duplication between ADR-0130 §Rationale ③ ↔ the qa binding trigger is handled separately (beware of confusion)** — it is not the "per-reader role split" of ① above (strategy/execution/entry/canonical) but the **two-copy ADR↔qa problem**, and the remedy differs: **the two command lines (regex · flags · paths) must be the same** (if they diverge one is wrong, so align them). Explanatory comments and prose have different readers so they need not be the same. **Only the *results* (0 lines · dates) may be frozen; a *command* is a tool, so its correctness has nothing to do with a date.** ★The draft blurred this and wrote "the ADR side is a snapshot at decision time so divergence is not a defect" and was **BLOCKed in review round 3** — ① that command was never the original text at decision time anyway (replaced twice in rounds 1 · 2) ② that framing would have suppressed the correct command replacement of round 1.★
- **Left unclosed:** whether to keep the `net → core` edge is a **code change**, so outside the document delegation (a user decision). The target is only 2 process liveness helpers under `agent::platform::` and it was judged non-blocking — nothing is blocked even if left alone.
- **★Process note★:** All three errors came from **edits that I judged to be "just one small document line"**. Being small is not a reason to exempt verification — especially a *sentence that warns of danger* reads plausibly even when its direction is flipped. Check factual claims mechanically before writing them.
- **Verification:** `/qa standard` all PASS (build · `--workspace --exclude engram-dashboard` 34 targets · fmt · tsc · vitest 41 files 634). **Since there were 0 source changes, this green is "the baseline is green", not "the change is safe"** — the real verification was the reviewer's fact check. GUI measurement not performed (frontend path unchanged = not a target of full).

## S18.26 CI introduction — verification gate automation + tag release (2026-08-09~11, master, conversation session) · `/review code full` 3 rounds 15 items applied · ADR-0131 · release `v0.1.0`

- **Motive:** There was **no CI at all**. The verification commands were all defined in CLAUDE.md, but every one was something a person had to remember to run, and especially the isolation gates (ADR-0003/0110/0129) are not enforced by the compiler and collapse silently. The discovery async intrusion incident (2026-08-05) happened exactly that way.
- **Result:** Full verification on every push + release on `v*` tags. Measured — gate 58s · backend 284s · frontend 100s · release build 634s · publish 9s. Artifact `engram-dashboard-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` (5.5MB). Decision and rejected alternatives = **ADR-0131**.
- **★3 findings by the adversarial review (all caught before the tag push)★:**
  - **The ts-rs binding gate was vacuous** — `cargo test -p engram-dashboard-protocol` only **regenerates** the bindings and `tests/ts_export.rs` has 0 assertions. CLAUDE.md advertises this command as the "codec golden + ts-rs bindings" gate, but **the wire↔TS drift axis passed green**. The frontend is a separate runner so it type-checks against the committed old `.ts`. Closed by appending `git diff --exit-code`.
  - **A public release could go out on a non-version tag** — the `tags: ['v*']` glob applies only to push, and `workflow_dispatch` can target an arbitrary ref. Put a name guard directly into the job `if`.
  - **The write token was in the same job as third-party code** — a compromised build dependency could plant a fake `gh` via `GITHUB_PATH`, steal the token, and finish pretending to succeed. Closed by **splitting into 2 jobs, build/publish** (ADR-0131 decision 4).
- **★Revealed only on the runner — the self skip guard does not work★:** The `skip_no_claude` guard of the 6 real-claude-dependent tests looks only at ① the spawn call succeeding ② appearing in the list within 5 seconds. Even when claude is absent the process starts at first and gets picked up in the list and then dies, so **the assertion breaks after passing the guard.** Which one blows up varies with timing (round 1 `c2_live_…`, round 2 `mcp_send_message_…` — different failures from the same code), so it went to exclusion by axis rather than per test. **The test source was not fixed — CI coverage of this axis is 0 and it is local-only.**
- **The review caught the asymmetry of pinning but not verifying** — rustc and ripgrep were pinned but there was no assertion that they actually arrived (if the file is deleted · `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` intervenes · the runner has a different rg, it silently runs a different version and goes green). Added a runtime assertion for both, and the rustc expected value is read from `rust-toolchain.toml` so **no second canonical source is created.** No separate assertion for the action SHA since GitHub enforces it.
- **★1 case where the coder expanded main's instruction with a justification (accepted)★:** Main instructed "give concurrency only to the release job and do not touch the workflow level", but **workflow-level `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels the whole run**, so a job-level group cannot prevent its own run's cancellation. Replaced with a form that turns cancellation off only on tag refs — branch · PR behavior unchanged.
- **Document reflection:** Added a CLAUDE.md 「CI」 section (the only surface through which the next session learns CI exists) · stated the division **local = quick + measurement / CI = the whole standard** in the `/qa` binding (user decision 2026-08-11) · ADR-0131.
- **Industry comparison (`/research` medium, based on the actual workflows of 15 projects — adversarial verification not performed):** Only 1 of 9 desktop apps runs GUI E2E on every PR (most are manual · smoke · none) — **leaving GUI out of CI is the majority position.** All 5 AI tools **mock the model HTTP**, so they never create the "skip if no binary" problem itself (to fit our form, it would be not a server but a **fake CLI**). The axes where we are above average = action SHA pinning (sample 6.3%) · minimized permissions (71.2% have no such block at all). **0 of 15 hang structural isolation gates in CI** — it is a convention specific to this project so there is nothing to compare against.
- **3 open items:** ① the 6 real-claude-dependent tests (as is / fake CLI harness / promote skip to failure) ② branch protection (revisit after observing CI stability) ③ bringing GUI measurement into CI — **there is no registered scenario** (`cdp.mjs` has only the 3 commands `shot`/`eval`/`info`, no suite concept). Writing scenarios is the real work and putting it on CI comes after.
- **Cleanup:** Deleted work branches `ci/github-actions` · `ci/release-job` (local · remote). Remainder = `wt2` (behind master) · 2 `worktree-agent-*` · remote `wip/a1` (identity unknown).

## S19.1 control plane CLI decision — a single executable `engram` with mail + control, isolation by daemon rejection (2026-08-11, `feat/control-cli`, conversation session) · ADR-0132 (0128 partially superseded) · **implementation is S19.2**

- **Motive:** While ADR-0128 hard-unified the mail channel, it **left the channel of the control plane (spawn etc.) undecided.** This time the user's tentative direction (「웬만하면 CLI」) was confirmed — control is low frequency so there is no reason to keep the tool schema resident in every agent's context (the grounds for mail being MCP do not apply to control).
- **★3 pre-start measurements split the scope★:**
  - **A control CLI surface already existed** — `src-tauri/src/cli.rs` doubles the release exe as a daemon control CLI and provides 4 verbs `list`/`send`/`spawn`/`kill` (reads daemon.json and connects directly over WS). So it was not "build new" but **"merge the surface that had split in two"**. Its `send` is stdin injection, a homonym with mail `send`.
  - **The UI relay is 0 lines of code** — ADR-0081 (`RegisterRole{UiApp}` + opaque-relay) is only a decision with 0 `.rs` hits (no role in `AuthFrame` · no relay arm in dispatch · no inbound handling in `src-tauri`). `docs/reference/architecture-overview.md` already admits it as "awaiting implementation (diff 0)". The daemon does not know `ViewManager` or layout vocabulary at all.
  - **No coordinate concept** — of the 17 window · tab · slot verbs in `layout.rs` · `popout.rs`, 0 take x/y/w/h. There is also no on-disk layout persistence (in-memory — initialized on client restart).
- **User decisions:** ① unify the entry (remove the app exe CLI mode + a separate executable `engram`) ② put mail + control in one executable and move isolation to **daemon rejection** ③ discovery = group help, priming is one line ④ control permission open to everyone (selective granting later) ⑤ put mail under the group too (symmetric — `engram mail send`) ⑥ position · size arguments are out of this scope.
- **Scope split in 3 (fixed by ADR-0132 decision 7):** ① agent control (= S19.2) → ② window · tab · slot **function** control (ADR-0081 relay implementation first) → ③ position · size (layout persistence first). The reason for splitting 1 and 2 is that the risk character differs — 1 is moving scattered names at once (silent send failure), 2 is laying wiring that did not exist. Mixing them prevents separating causes.
- **★ADR-0132 decision 3 is a state where only the document went ahead — the code is still the old means★:** It confirmed "move the isolation means to daemon rejection" and even stamped a supersession on ADR-0128, but **the rejection code is built in the mail rejection gate piece within round 1** (after the control verb piece · before the app CLI teardown — a different numbering system from round 3 of 「범위 3분할」 above. They have been misread by overlapping). Until then, what actually isolates mail is still only the `claude.rs` branch "do not inject CLI wiring into MCP-capable spawns". If someone reads only the stamp and deletes that branch, isolation becomes 0 — ADR-0132 §Impact states "do not delete" explicitly. **2 of the 3 deep reviewers found it independently** (a defect main created while writing the ADR — it did not record the time lag between decision and implementation).
  - **★The item above was superseded in S19.5 on 2026-08-12 — a session reading this now must not follow it★:** That branch is gone ("wiring goes to everyone") and the "do not delete" clause of ADR-0132 §Impact was erased at the same time. The current enforcement = **solely** the credential rejection of the daemon auth middleware. If you revive that branch on the strength of the sentence above, the control path of MCP-capable spawns is cut (violates ADR-0132 decision 5). Canonical source = ADR-0133 §Impact.
- **ADR-0086 stamp deferred (judgment):** "workers get only send_message" is about the MCP tool axis so there is no wording conflict with this decision on the CLI axis, and 0086 itself anticipated an additive follow-up of control verbs. Only the tension in tone was left in ADR-0132 §Impact and no stamp was applied (3 reasons = that item).
- **Tool defect 1 (recurred for the 8th time):** `index --write` of `adr.mjs` **silently deleted the second amendment mark** in the index cell of an ADR that received 2 or more partial supersessions (0099 · 0108 · 0111 · 0112 · 0113 · 0116 — 6 rows). After manual recovery, confirmed by diff that only the intended 2 rows remain. Accumulated in skill feedback the new observation of this round (= it can be detected immediately just by reading `action:"rewritten"` in the script's JSON).

## S19.2 Piece ① — rename the mail CLI to the integrated tool `engram` + group structure + group help (2026-08-11, `feat/control-cli`, conversation→autonomous mix) · coder 5 rounds · `/review code deep` 4 rounds (9 reviewer runs) · `/qa full` PASS (CLI-only round-trip measurement with 2 real agents)

- **What:** `engram-send` → `engram` (bin · file · test rename). Flat surface (implicit default verb + `status`/`pending`) → **group structure** `engram mail send|status|pending`. Added **group help** (`engram` · `engram help` · `engram help mail` · `--help`/`-h` — answers **before** the credential check so the surface is discoverable even outside a spawn). Converged name · group · flags · verb vocabulary into **core constants** (`CLI_EXE_NAME` · `CLI_GROUP_MAIL` · `CLI_MAIL_FLAGS` · `CLI_MAIL_VERBS`) — 0 Rust literal duplication. `ENGRAM_SEND_EXE` → `ENGRAM_CLI_EXE`. **Mail meaning · wire · the exit code 3-way split are unchanged** — only the spelling that is called changed.
- **★What the adversarial review found — the character differed each round★:**
  - **1R (design):** ① the name became shorter so the grant prefix **now covers sibling executables too** (`engram-dashboard*`) ② **the document went ahead of the code** — ADR-0132 decision 3 (daemon rejection) was confirmed and even stamped on ADR-0128, but the rejection code is unimplemented, so a session that read only the stamp could delete the only isolation branch.
  - **2R (behavior):** a path where the help **silently drops the message** · the detector was pierced by case · newlines · markdown.
  - **3R (gate):** plain prose `The Engram mailbox…` was a **false positive** for the detector — no word boundary.
  - **4R (latent bug):** if a value is missing as in `--body --body-stdin`, it **swallows the following flag as the value, drops the piped body, and exits 0**. Found solely by the cross-family reviewer — the Claude-family reviewer judged the same round as "comments only". **The value of splitting families came out here.**
- **★2 cases the coder refused main's instruction with justification (both accepted)★:** ① the instruction to widen the detection scope to the whole group — control verbs are taught to every spawn, so the tool name cannot be the basis for discriminating the mail channel, and widening would reject every MCP experiment or become "mail was not taught yet it passes". Both reviewers independently confirmed "the coder is right". ② the instruction to demote environment variable mentions to a trace signal — the form `$ENGRAM_CLI_EXE mail send` **does not show the executable name** (the real incident form recorded by ADR-0098). Instead, defined **calling token + group + verb adjacency** as teaching.
- **★1 guard test — the user removed it, then it was revived on review grounds★:** The shipped executable name ↔ constant cross-check. It was first dropped as "it surfaces anyway", but the review pointed out that **a combination that renames only the constant and the guidance text and misses the manifest shows up nowhere**. A manifest rename is caught at compile time by the `CARGO_BIN_EXE_` macro, so **one line covers both directions**. The counterargument that Cargo auto-discovery neutralizes this binding was **refuted by the coder measuring it in an isolated copy** (if an explicit target occupies the path it is not regenerated).
- **★Measurement = the axis CI cannot do★:** Launched 2 real claudes (A · B) with `roundtrip-smoke --cli-only` and forced provision to non-MCP → **B called `engram mail send` on its own** (`B_SENT=true ENTRANCE=cli`), all 3 deliveries CLI entrance · delivered. It proves that the rename · guidance · grant · PATH alignment really hold. CI has no claude on the runner and can never cover this axis. The ADR-0130 revisit trigger was also checked locally — the outgoing edges of `control/` stay at 0 lines.
- **★The review was deliberately cut off at round 5★:** Each round got lighter (design defect → behavior bug → gate hole → comment wording), and fixing a comment makes that comment a review target again — a **self-proliferating structure** with no natural end point. The last round's result was not re-reviewed and was left to the CI regression (user judgment — 「왜 이렇게 오래 걸리냐」). It was a post-hoc judgment that it should have been cut at 3R, but the loss bug of 4R also refutes that judgment.
- **1 open item registered:** T-19 — the lookup decision treats an empty response (`200 {}`) as success too (a pre-existing defect). Changing the exit code contract in the middle of the rename would prevent separating the regression cause, so it was deferred.
- **Documents:** In ADR-0132 §Impact, stated "decision 3 unimplemented — do not delete the old means" + acceptance of the grant prefix expansion + the revisit trigger. Marked the CLI argument block of `spec §6` as superseded (the response shape section remains valid — code citations were also split by axis and re-aimed). The overlap between piece numbers and round numbers that caused misreading was spelled out in both documents.

## S19.3 Piece ② — agent control endpoint (`/control/agent`) + CLI `agent` group (2026-08-11, `feat/control-cli`, autonomous session) · coder 3 rounds · `/review code full` 2 rounds (4 reviewer runs) · `/qa` local gate PASS

- **What:** Added `/control/agent` to the daemon HTTP control plane (**the same router · the same bearer middleware** as the existing `/control/send`, with the verb in the body). Five verbs = `list` · `spawn` (wake by name / create and launch new with `--cwd`) · `new` (register only) · `rename` · `move` (change parent). The CLI gets the `agent` group + `engram help agent`. **0 duplication of manager logic** — it calls the same methods the WS path calls.
- **★`kill` and `rm` were left out (user decision)★** — their semantics are entangled (deleting does not kill the process, which conflicts with ADR-0122, and that implementation is undecided). The rationale and the gap in the meantime are recorded in ADR-0132 §Impact. **That gap = an agent can launch but cannot stop via the CLI.**
- **★What the review caught — its character differed per round★:**
  - **1R:** ① **The response lied about state** — it discarded the real status and hard-coded a `"live"` literal, so an agent that died while waking was reported as "started" while `list` answered "sleeping" for the same agent (two verbs on the same endpoint contradicting each other). ② **`move` folded an empty value, a missing field, and a typo all into "no parent"**, so a single typo silently detached an agent from the tree. ③ The cross-family reviewer returned **BLOCK** — unbounded creation had no limit, a wake revived a profile that had been deleted concurrently, and a spawn during shutdown was missing from the list.
  - **2R:** the cap was **route-local, so the WS path bypassed it**, and the check was non-atomic · the decider **passed contradictory evidence** (a wake with `created:true`) · **`list` returned a combination that was never committed** (old name + new parent) · **the regression test for the round-1 defect failed to catch the defect**.
- **★Three core fixes★:** ① **Moved the cap into the core** — both new-registration points check **inside the name-assignment gate**, so it is atomic and independent of the entry point. Existing agents, restore, and respawn are never blocked (pinned by a test). In the test where 8 threads race for the last free spot, exactly 1 passes. ② **State is derived only** — extracted into the pure functions `state_of` + `spawn_payload` and verified by feeding terminal states directly. **Reverting to the literal turned the test red (tamper) — confirmed.** ③ **`roster()` reads only once** — the old path's per-session `profiles.get` (mutex + full clone) is gone, so **the mail-send critical path actually got cheaper.**
- **★3 items the coder rejected with reasons — the reviewer confirmed all of them as "correct"★:** a deletion revived during wake · a spawn missed during shutdown · a registry save failure reported as success. All three **cannot be closed inside `control/`** (wherever the check goes it sits outside the lock, so it only narrows the window and makes things look safe); they require changing the manager lifecycle and save contract, and **the WS path suffers the same pre-existing problem.** What is needed was also retrieved and registered as T-20, T-21, and T-22.
- **Boundary preservation confirmed:** the ADR-0130 leaf (0 lines — fan-out is inverted into a `control/`-owned port + a `connection_core` adapter to keep it one-directional) · the ADR-0119 vocabulary (no "profile" anywhere in wire, hints, help, or output) · ADR-0132 §Impact: mail isolation branch, priming, and spawn wiring unchanged · the 3 isolation gates.
- **★Cut the review off at round 2★:** reflecting the experience (the user's remark) that piece ① went up to 4 rounds and the later rounds dragged on over comment wording, we declared a cap of 2 at kickoff and kept to it. The last fixes are left to CI regression without an adversarial review — the judgment and its reason are recorded here.

## S19.4 piece ③ decision — the list is split by caller (a marker set at spawn), and a refusal does not name an alternative channel (2026-08-12, `wt2`, conversation session) · ADR-0133 · **implementation not started**

- **Why a decision was needed now:** opening control to everyone requires wiring the single executable into every spawn, and that executable also carries the mail family. On top of that, with decision 4 (discovery = group help), **this is the first time agents are taught to "look at the list"** — if the list is the same for everyone, "don't teach it", which ADR-0128 named as the primary control, collapses in this round. The user's remark showed that the daemon refusal (ADR-0132 decision 3) alone is only half of it.
- **3 decisions (all user):** ① the list **differs by caller** — the mail family does not appear in `engram help` for MCP-capable agents ② the means of splitting is **one environment-variable marker injected at spawn** — the CLI reads it locally and splits the render (it does not query the daemon to produce the list → keeps piece ①'s "answers before the credential check") ③ **the refusal response does not name an alternative channel** — only as far as "mail is not possible with this credential". If a problem is observed, we revisit then (user: 「그냥 못 쓴다고 해」).
- **★The basis for a rejection was overturned — the user's question caught it★:** At first we cited "the marker approach shows the list even if the daemon dies" as a strength, but measurement showed that **when the daemon dies, child agents also die with it via `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`**, so a "daemon-less agent" does not exist. Availability cannot be a reason for rejection; the real reasons are these three: **① a policy is newly needed for no-response ② help gains an authentication and communication path ③ a human cannot read the usage without the daemon.** This correction was written explicitly into the ADR-0133 Rejected alternatives.
- **3 measurements:** help is a pure local render that only substitutes constant strings (0 network or authentication paths) · the CLI does not assert identity (no `--as` or similar; identity is derived by the daemon from the token — ADR-0086) · the injection site already exists in `inject_cli_entrance`, and 3 tests seal that MCP spawns do not call it.
- **Invariant shift:** the "teaching = wiring" equality breaks and **reverts to "teaching ⊆ wiring"** (wiring is for everyone, only the list is split). Since ADR-0132 §Impact **already** stamped the partial-discard mark on the isolation means of ADR-0128 decisions 2 and 3, we did not add a new stamp — ADR-0133 is the executable form of that replacement.
- **★Fixed at the root the index defect that had recurred for the 9th time (user instruction)★:** The index status-field derivation in `adr.mjs` read only **the first** `Amended by` link on the related line (non-g `.match()`), so every regeneration silently erased the second qualifier of an ADR that had received 2 or more amendments. This time 6 (0099 · 0108 · 0111 · 0112 · 0113 · 0116) were erased and restored by hand, and after fixing it with `matchAll`, **8 more that nobody had known about surfaced** (0019 · 0066 · 0076 · 0094 · 0103 · 0107 · 0112 · 0115 — the notation had been missing from long ago). Next we fixed a second defect with the same root: the clause end was cut at **the first closing parenthesis**, so a clause containing a parenthesis was cut in the middle of a word (13 cases); we replaced it with a **balanced-parenthesis scan** — truncation warnings 13 → 0. Final = rewritten 0 · truncation 0 · lint error 0 (the 2 advisories are pre-existing legacy).
  - **The script is owned by the global `adr` skill**, so the fix also went there (outside this repository). We note it here so the next session does not look for "it was fixed in this project".
- **Session operation change (user decision):** the branch is fixed to **the name of the worktree the session was launched from** — a main-folder session is `wt1`, a wt2-folder session is `wt2`. No new topic branch is created, and master integration is per chunk. This convention was not in the docs, so a session created a topic branch out of habit, which caused this drift; we wrote one line into CLAUDE.md 「구현 실행 규약」(`2f4cff5`). `feat/control-cli` was advanced by name only to `wt2` without a rewind (ancestor-descendant relationship confirmed), and 4 leftover branches and 2 old remote names were cleaned up.

## S19.5 piece ③ — move mail isolation to a daemon refusal + wire the CLI into all spawns (2026-08-12, `wt2`, autonomous session) · commit `9ebdb15` · coder 3 rounds · `/review code deep` 3 rounds (6 reviewer runs) · `/qa full` PASS (including GUI measurement)

- **What:** Implemented ADR-0133. `inject_cli_entrance` runs on **every** control-endpoint spawn, and for MCP-capable spawns `--mcp-config` goes **along with it** (the two are no longer mutually exclusive). Enforcement is solely the `TokenBinding.mail_allowed` refusal in the `bearer_auth` middleware. The decision is computed **once** by `provision` via `accepts_mcp_config` and fed to the credential and the marker at the same time (a single derivation point · reissued on epoch rotation). Teaching only splits the help render via the `ENGRAM_MAIL=on|off` marker and **does not block execution**.
- **★The warning sentence of S19.1 was discarded by this step★** — that entry wrote "what actually isolates mail is still only the non-MCP-only wiring branch in `claude.rs`, and ADR-0132 §Impact states 'do not delete' explicitly", but **both are now false**: that branch is gone and that clause was also deleted this time. A session that reaches that sentence first by grepping `우편 격리` and **"restores" the removed branch would cut the control path of MCP-capable spawns entirely** (violates ADR-0132 decision 5). The current authority = ADR-0133 §Impact.
- **★What the review caught — its character differed per round★:**
  - **1R (3 reviewers: doc-aware + blind + coverage audit):** blind returned **BLOCK** — the test knob `ENGRAM_FORCE_CLI_ONLY_SEND` was compiled into release and now **flips the authorization decision** (a pre-existing knob, but this change widened its blast radius). doc-aware ran the real binary and reproduced **the hidden family leaking through an argument error** (the single word `engram mail` returned the entire verb list — more than the help screen gives). The endpoint-classification guarantee is actually a convention, yet a comment **overstated** it as "the compiler prevents this". The core gate test **fed in the decision value by hand**, so it stayed green even if every real classification was wrong.
  - **2R:** all 11 items confirmed CLOSED (doc-aware found the knob string **0 times** in the release binary, with a control proving the search was valid). Remaining = a path **after** parsing slipping through the net and leaking the single `--body` flag.
  - **3R (narrowed):** the prefix comparison folding `/controlfoo` across a segment boundary.

## S20 — release data under the run folder + single instance by a connection-key file lock (2026-08-14, `wt1`, mixed conversation + autonomous) · commit `485f84c` · while implementing ADR-0134, **ADR-0135 created (design reversed twice)** · coder 6 rounds · `/review code deep` 5 rounds (14 reviewer runs) · `/research medium` once · local gates PASS · **GUI and release zip measurement not performed**

- **What:** Release data goes to `engram-data/` next to the executable instead of `%APPDATA%` (fully portable). Single instance is decided by holding `daemon.json` in that folder with a restricted share mode (`FILE_SHARE_READ` alone) — **the lock file and the connection key are one file**. If the data folder cannot be written, it fails with no fallback, and the dashboard pre-checks before startup and shows the reason in the window.
- **★The design was reversed twice — that history is the core of this step★:** ① `/research` refuted the previous session's **path fingerprint + named mutex** (there is no need to identify the folder — if you lock a file inside the folder, the OS resolves path aliases) → ADR-0134 decision 3 ② When that file lock was built as a **range lock**, it blocked others' **reads too**, so copying the distribution folder failed → switched to share mode ③ Once deletion was blocked, **the daemon became an orphan after the folder was deleted** (it could neither be attached to nor stopped) → we added daemon self-recovery, but **the user rejected it with 「지운 게 되살아나는 건 원하는 동작이 아니다」** → `/research medium` refuted the two-file structure itself → **ADR-0135 (merge)**.
- **★What the research overturned — all 3 symptom-handling options were wrong★:** Self-recovery had been **reported as a bug in every case surveyed** (VS Code · Zed · rclone · GitHub Desktop — GitHub Desktop in particular objected **even when the content was byte-identical**), and the only line where reviving is acceptable is caches (XDG). For voluntary exit (the PostgreSQL way), adversarial verification **refuted the analogy** — what Postgres watches is **the interlock itself**, and its exit is **an emergency exit that needs recovery**. For the notify-only option, **the PID to kill was in the deleted file**. The answer adversarial verification produced was "**the missing dominant option: if a file that cannot be deleted carries the connection info, the orphan state itself never arises**" — PostgreSQL `postmaster.pid` has exactly that structure.
- **★The main session gave the coder a wrong instruction and the coder refuted it with measurement★:** It instructed the share flags as `FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE` (=3), but `FILE_SHARE_WRITE` means **"allow other processes to open for write"**, so **a second daemon simply gets in**. Had it gone that way, the single-instance guarantee would have silently vanished. The coder attached a probe table and corrected it to `FILE_SHARE_READ` alone, and a separate reviewer independently re-measured with their own probe and confirmed it. **There were also 2 cases where the line numbers in the reviewer's citation were stale and the coder rightly rebutted.**
- **★OS-lens measurement (separate reviewer)★:** 8 alias kinds (uppercase · `..` · `\\?\` · 8.3 short names · junction · hardlink · `subst` · mapped drive vs UNC) **all converge on one file object** and yield 32. On **2 real SMB shares**, exclusion, client reads, and delete denial all hold (the redirector propagates ShareAccess and the server arbitrates). The same on a OneDrive sync root. Re-acquisition after a forced kill **38~48ms, on the first attempt**. Unmeasured = FAT32/exFAT/ReFS (no volume) · third-party redirectors (WebDAV · Dokan/WinFsp — here enforcement is **the filesystem's jurisdiction** so it can be defeated, stated in the header).
- **★2 "silently breaking" things the review caught★:** ① If a **read-only attribute** is attached to the file (backup restore · copy from read-only media · antivirus action), the open fails with **5** instead of 32 and exits with no retry — the release daemon has no console, so it becomes a **permanent timeout with no cause** → if only the attribute is the problem, clear it once and retry; otherwise classify as a separate error ② The clean regeneration in `build-release.ps1` **stops partway through deletion**, wiping only `agents.json` and not even building (launching with `실행.bat` and then `빌드.bat` is the ordinary path) → check for in-use files before deleting and refuse.
- **2 pre-existing defects found:** a race between the two lookups in the folder write check (that test **failed 4 out of 20 times even before my change** — "all gates green" was actually flaky) · `scripts/engram.mjs` cannot tolerate the newly created torn-read window.
- **Removed:** path fingerprint · normalization · `Global\` named mutex · `ENGRAM_INSTANCE_KEY` · `instance.lock` · `write_atomic` · `try_lock` · the direct `windows` dependency · the connection-key self-recovery task · the portfile `data_dir` field · the dedicated exit-code wiring. **Invalidation stamps on 3 dead clauses in ADR-0134 §Impact.**
- **Gates:** full regression **0 failures** (backend) · net both features (42/6) · fmt · 5 isolation gates + core tauri 0 + messaging 0 · bindings drift clean · `tsc` clean · vitest **42 files 647 cases** · real-process e2e passed (excluding the known pre-existing failure `daemon_kill_cleans_pty_child`) · **real daemon measurement** (read while held OK · delete · rename · folder move refused · second daemon exit 0 with the record unchanged · clean re-acquisition after kill).
- **What was not done:** GUI measurement · actually building the release zip to confirm that the distribution and a debug daemon coexist · `cargo clippy` (not installed locally, CI's jurisdiction).

## S20.4 Step 2 slice 3 — replace the 5-verb wall of `/control/agent` with a table lookup (2026-08-16, `wt2`, autonomous session) · coder 6 fix rounds · 6 adversarial review passes · **uncommitted · `/qa full` = PARTIAL**

- **What:** The daemon's HTTP `/control/agent` dropped the hand-written 5-verb match (`list` · `spawn` · `new` · `rename` · `move`) and ~20 helpers that had twins in core, and now finds and calls `agent.<verb>` in the table assembled by `make_daemon_table`. ~600 lines of wall removed. The entrance adds only three things — `{verb}` → command-name assembly · the entrance argument check (ADR-0157 `check_args` — set up together while swapping the table) · the table's outcome → wire envelope.
- **★With user approval, the wire changed in two places — this piece is not 「동작 불변」★:** ① the success payload goes from nested (`{"agent":{id,name,state}}`) to the table's flat Ok struct (`{agent_id,name,state,created}` and so on) ② the error `code` goes from domain strings to the tool crate's typed `ErrorCode` wire strings (`AGENT_NOT_FOUND`→`NOT_FOUND` · `AGENT_AMBIGUOUS`·`MOVE_REJECTED`·`ROSTER_FULL`·`NAME_SPACE_EXHAUSTED`→`CONFLICT` · `SPAWN_FAILED`→`INTERNAL` · `INVALID_AGENT_ARGS`→`INVALID_ARGUMENT` · unknown verb→`UNKNOWN_COMMAND`). **Unchanged:** the envelope structure (`{status,code,hint}` · `status:"error"`) · the property that a runnable command is attached to the hint tail · the exit code of `engram agent <verb>` and the outcome the user sees. Slice 2 pre-laid the flat-shape reading in the CLI, and removing the nested reading is slice 4. **We corrected the verification line of TRD §6 Step 2 with this fact — do not use that line as grounds to revert the door to the nested shape.**
- **Cross-check net repair:** The test that checked whether the control door and the mail entrance resolve the target token the same way was running the daemon's **dead copy** (`resolve_target`/`TargetResolution`). We raised core `resolve_in` to `pub` so that test drives **the resolver the door actually uses**, and deleted the daemon copy.
- **The preceding Step 2 pieces (0 · 2 · 5a · 1, commits `e26ec8d` · `aecf50b`) have 0 wiring, so they have no separate entry — this piece is the first behavior change of Step 2.**
- **Verification = `/qa full` PARTIAL (run 2026-08-16).** **What ran:** build · full workspace regression (0 failures) · `cargo fmt --check` · 3 isolation gates (core tauri 0 · messaging 0 · tool crate direct dependency 1 line) · ts-rs bindings sync · discovery async 0 · 0 lines of the ADR-0130 revisit trigger. **The release profile was also run** (the first time in this repo): all integration targets passed (including `control_agent` 23), lib 226 passed · **the 2 failures are pre-existing defects** (㉱ below). **GUI measurement = partial:** app and daemon launch, dashboard connection, tree render, and real operation of IPC `agent_spawn`/`agent_kill`/`agent_write_stdin` were confirmed, and `/control/agent` is alive and returns 401. **★We ran the five verbs through the real CLI against a live daemon (the first time in this repo)★** — the shell backend has no token injection (㉲), so we woke a claude profile and ran `engram agent` with the endpoint and token from its mcp-config. `list` flat rows exit 0 · `new` **flat payload** `{agent_id,name,state}` exit 0 · `rename` `{…,outcome:"renamed"}` exit 0 · `move --parent none` detach to top level `parent:null` exit 0 · `move` to a nonexistent parent → **`code:"NOT_FOUND"` (typed vocabulary) + envelope `{status,code,hint}` + a runnable `` `engram agent list` `` on the hint tail + exit 1**. The two approved wire changes and the contract we committed to keep were confirmed on the real thing. **What could not be done = live confirmation of four things: entrance argument refusal (ADR-0157), unknown verb, duplicate key, and move to a real parent** — credentials are reissued on every spawn and the dev app kept exiting on its own (㉳), so the token kept being invalidated. The changed handler itself is covered in both debug and release by 23 real HTTP integration tests.
- **★㉱ 2 daemon lib tests break in release — pre-existing and unrelated to this piece★:** `resolve_data_dir_delegates_to_discovery_local_dir` · `resolve_data_dir_honors_env_override` (`crates/engram-dashboard-daemon/src/lib.rs`). The first asserts a **debug-only assumption** (the data folder ends with `.engram-data`) while the release path is `%APPDATA%\com.engram.dashboard`, so it fails, and the second **fails as a cascade from lock poisoning** because the first panicked while holding `ENV_LOCK` (not an independent failure). It went unnoticed because this repo had never run release tests. To fix it, either change to a profile-aware assertion or split with `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`.
- **㉲ Shell-backend agents cannot use the `engram` CLI (pre-existing, measured 2026-08-16).** In that agent's shell `engram` is not on PATH, and even invoked by absolute path it is bounced with `NO_TOKEN` — because the `ENGRAM_TOKEN` · `ENGRAM_CONTROL_URL` injection exists only for the claude backend. The priming document tells agents "use `engram` in your shell", so **the document and reality diverge by backend.**
- **㉳ The dev app (`npm run tauri dev`) repeatedly exits on its own — cause not identified, unrelated to this piece (measured 2026-08-16).** During measurement it died twice (exit 1 · `0xffffffff`) with no reason in the log, and the first time it took the daemon down with it. The app **does not call** the `/control/agent` we changed **at all** — the only production caller of that door is the `engram` CLI (confirmed by tracing the whole repo). So there is no causal link, but it was the direct reason GUI measurement could not be pushed to the end, so we leave it. If it reproduces, it is a separate issue.

## S21 — dev and release coexistence + a path that leaves the reason in release (2026-08-16, `wt1`, mixed conversation + autonomous) · commits `fd89e39..156aa17` · ADR-0137 · 0138 · 0139 (recorded after the fact in this step) · distribution measurement PASS

- **What (5 items):** ① **a separate bundle identifier for the dev build** (`com.engram.dashboard.dev` — `scripts/tauri-cli.mjs` injects the overlay `src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json` only into the `dev` subcommand) ② **release file log** (the daemon and the app shell each write `<데이터 폴더>/logs/<종류>-<UTC>-<pid>.log`, synchronous writes, 10 kept per kind) ③ **each of the two launchers kills only its own distribution's daemon** (triple check of connection-key pid + image name + exe path, re-check after kill) ④ **control CLI connection-failure diagnostics** (prints the reason, the chosen connection key, and the candidate list) ⑤ **real implementation of `CDP_MATCH`** (the tree and pop-out windows also became measurement targets).
- **★Why dev died — the mutex name comes from the identifier★:** When the release app was running, the dev app **exited immediately with neither a window nor its own daemon** (the dev connection key was byte-identical before and after the run). This is because `tauri-plugin-single-instance` creates the Windows global mutex as `{identifier}-sim`, and checking the plugin source (2.4.2/2.4.3) showed that the Builder exposes only `callback` and the **Linux-only** `dbus_id`, so **overriding the name is impossible** — splitting the identifier was the only lever. → ADR-0137.
- **★In release, stdout goes nowhere (three layers)★:** a no-console subsystem · WMI `Win32_Process.Create` **cannot pass std handles** (the non-WMI path gets null outright) · the daemon does not inherit the parent environment, so **`RUST_LOG` does not reach it**. So the only thing left to the user was the single banner `데몬 시작 대기 timeout(5s 초과)`. **Confirmed that an async writer must not be adopted** — the daemon ends with `std::process::exit` and skips destructors, so **the last line just before a startup failure** left in the buffer vanishes exactly (crate check: default buffer 128,000 lines · default lossy · shutdown timeout 100ms/1000ms). → ADR-0138.
- **★Killing by image name was killing other people's work★:** `taskkill /IM engram-dashboard-daemon.exe /F` killed **every daemon on the machine**, and since agents are children of the daemon (ADR-0029), running the release launcher during development **destroyed in-progress agent work** (measured). ① made running dev and release at the same time the norm, which enlarged the blast radius further, so we fixed it in the same batch. The dev launcher had **the very same line**, so the option of fixing only one side did not hold up. → ADR-0139.
- **★What the review caught★:** the **file sink installation failure was silent** (`7f0fd5c`) — the situation where the primary folder cannot be written is exactly where diagnostics are most needed, yet only then did the reason go to stdout (which does not exist in release). Since dev and release use different single-instance lock names, coexistence is actually reachable.

## S22 — redefine split-direction vocabulary + empty-slot affordance (2026-08-17, `wt3`, conversation) · commit `b30f230` · ADR-0140 · 0141 created · GUI measurement PASS

- **What (3 items):** ① **Renamed the split-direction vocabulary by resulting placement** — `SplitDir { Horizontal, Vertical }` → `{ LeftRight, TopBottom }` (wire `"left_right"`/`"top_bottom"`), command id `slot.split.h/v` → `slot.split.topBottom/leftRight`, i18n keys `splitH/splitV` → `splitTopBottom/splitLeftRight`. The Korean label strings and menu order are unchanged and **only the meaning flipped** — `가로 분할` = top/bottom, `세로 분할` = left/right. ② **Empty slot = a central `+` icon alone** (removed the two lines `Slot <id8>` · `— empty —`, deleted the `common.viewEmpty` key). Clicking opens the menu in the same state and the same component as right-click. ③ **Menu edge position correction changed from pushing to flipping**.
- **★Why we did not just flip the labels★:** The user report was 「가로/세로가 반대」 and the minimal fix is reversing the label↔direction mapping by one line. But `horizontal`/`vertical` **cannot be decided from the name alone as to which convention** (tmux = left-right, vim = top-bottom). If only the mapping is flipped, the `Horizontal = 좌우` comment in `types.rs` stays alive while the `가로 분할` menu sends `Vertical`, and the mismatch between name and behavior is **the very cause of this report** — it becomes a coordinate by which the next session reads it as a bug and reverts. So we changed the vocabulary to the resulting placement so that the name states the result. → ADR-0140.
- **★We removed `+` from the tab order — an intended absence★:** 2 reviewers independently caught that the `+` built as a native button opened **the first path by which the keyboard reaches the slot menu**. That menu supports neither item execution nor Esc dismissal (a pre-existing defect, the same on the right-click path), so you cannot get out without a mouse. User decision = exclude from the order. **The option of adding keyboard operation to the menu was rejected** — that defect was not made by this affordance but was originally in the right-click path, so fixing it here blurs ownership. However, `tabIndex=-1` does not remove the element from the accessibility tree, so **the screen-reader path remains** — ADR-0141 states this residual path and the release condition (at least Esc on the menu first) together.
- **★The path by which a double-click executed a menu item★:** When the menu overflowed the viewport we **pushed** it inside, but then the anchor (the pressed point) goes inside the menu and an item sits under the cursor. It was harmless in the right-click days, but `+` is a left-click opener, so the following double-click executes that item — and if `닫기` happens to be there, the slot disappears. We changed from pushing to **flipping** so the anchor always sits at a menu corner, and it applies to the right-click path too (we do not split position rules per opener).
- **★The review caught a record error★:** The ADR-0140 draft wrote "CI's ts-rs bindings sync gate catches `src-tauri/bindings/` drift", but **that gate covers only the protocol crate bindings**. Moreover, the generator for that folder (`export_bindings_*`) belongs to the `engram-dashboard` package, which is excluded from both local and CI tests, and the target itself dies with `0xc0000139` — so this folder was **already stale at HEAD**. Recording a nonexistent safety net as existing makes the next rename skip hand editing. After the correction we stamped into ADR-0140 "aligned by hand and confirmed only by GUI measurement".
- **Verification:** `cargo build` · `cargo test --workspace --exclude engram-dashboard` · `cargo fmt --check` · all isolation gates (core · messaging · net 1~5 · ADR-0130 trigger · discovery async · protocol bindings sync) · `tsc` · vitest 656 · **GUI measurement 8 items PASS** (release build, pane coordinates measured — `가로 분할` → left identical · top differs, `세로 분할` → top identical · left differs, the anchor is outside the menu on edge flipping).
- **★The structural hole the measurement demonstrated★:** The `engram-dashboard` (src-tauri) package tests **run nowhere, neither local nor CI** (the workspace test excludes it + the target dies with `0xc0000139`). `cargo build` does not even compile `#[cfg(test)]` bodies. The Rust half of this change (`layout/{types,tree,spatial,manager}.rs`) had **GUI measurement as its only observation point**. A pre-existing constraint, not created this time — registered as T-27 in `docs/tracking.md`.
- **What was not done:** the reviewer's 4 lows (the same fact living in both the code comment and the test comment, a duplication) not applied — no behavioral impact. The release exe used for GUI measurement has a QA-only bundle identifier baked in, so an ordinary rebuild is needed before distribution.
- **★Same-day follow-up (2026-08-17/18) — redesign of the empty-slot click target + double-click destruction defect★** (commit `v0.2.0/fix/empty-slot-click`, ADR-0143 created · 0141 partially superseded). The user, seeing the implementation, instructed that it should be a left-click **anywhere in the empty slot**, not only on the icon → we demoted `+` from a button to **a pure graphic** (`pointer-events:none` · 44px) and merged click handling into the slot container. As a side effect, the **3 items that ADR-0141 had covered with the tab-order exclusion — keyboard trap · click without coordinates · dedicated accessible name — vanished along with their grounds** (with no button, nothing enters the order).
- **★That enlarged target opened a destruction defect — the review caught it★:** Because the menu anchor was **stuck right at the menu corner**, double-clicking an empty slot had the first click open the menu and the **second click execute an item**. Lower on the screen the menu flips upward so the bottom-most `닫기` lands under the cursor and **the slot disappears with no means to undo it** (layouts have no disk persistence). In the old structure the target was a central 32px icon so flipping was rare and it lay dormant. → We separated the anchor and menu with `ANCHOR_GAP=8` (derivation = Windows `SM_CXDOUBLECLK` default 4px → 4 times the 2px tolerance radius. Not an arbitrary value). **ADR-0141's "the anchor does not go inside the menu" allowed even touching the boundary and fell short — 0142 strengthened it with a gap clause.**
- **★The review also caught 2 factual errors in the ADR itself★:** ① The first edition of 0143 wrote "with no button there is no click without coordinates either", but that path **moved from the button to the slot** and is still alive (if code calls `.click()` on the slot the menu opens at the viewport top-left — we left it dormant since there is no call site, it did not go away). ② "A left-click does not reposition while the menu is open" read as unconditional, but in fact **inside and outside the menu differ** (outside = a margin click deliberately moves it — it depends on the order in which outside-click dismissal runs first on `mousedown`). Both corrected in the body.
- **Verification:** vitest 661 · tsc clean · Rust unchanged (0-line difference from master, machine-checked) · **GUI measurement 10 items PASS** (release bundle, page URL `tauri.localhost` confirmed). The double-click was tested with **6 jitter combinations in the dangerous direction (upper right)**, and we first confirmed that `닫기` actually deletes the slot, so we **also verified that the test does not spin idle**. In each of the 6 mutation checks only the intended test failed.
- **★2 measurement pitfalls (reflected in the qa binding)★:** ① If **another worktree is holding** the dev server (1420), you measure that screen and misjudge it as a pass — the app looks normal so there is no clue. Before reuse, check the owning worktree from the command line, and if it is someone else's, do not kill it but switch to the release path. ② Then **a plain `cargo build --release` falls into the same trap as is** (it still loads `localhost:1420`) — the exe that holds the screen is built by `npm run tauri build -- --no-bundle`. ③ vite is a separate process from the app, so **it keeps holding 1420 even after the app is closed, and there was no cleanup clause** — added with the same ownership rule as the daemon.
- **What was not done (follow-up):** a regression that re-attaches `onClick` to the icon **cannot be caught by a test** (React delegates handlers to the root so `element.onclick` is always null, and the two handlers use the same coordinates so a double open is invisible behaviorally) — that clause depends on review alone.

## S22 — mail delivery parallelized per recipient + introduction of a second concurrency-exclusion axis (2026-08-18, `fix/tui-message-submit`, conversation session) · commit `c2e56cb` (not merged to master) · ADR-0142 · `/review code deep` 3 rounds (3 adversarial reviewers: doc-aware invariant destroyer · cross-family blind destroyer · concurrency/teardown lens) · `/qa full` PASS (2 measurements)

- **What:** Parallelized mail delivery per recipient (flush lane → per-recipient dispatcher) and newly added in-flight exclusion on the target axis (including the caller-scoped `DrainReport` decision). 2 files — `crates/engram-dashboard-daemon/src/messaging_host.rs` (flush lane → per-recipient dispatcher) · `crates/engram-dashboard-messaging/src/service.rs` (target-axis in-flight exclusion + caller-scoped decision). Rationale and rejected alternatives = ADR-0142.
- **Review:** `/review code deep` 3 rounds, adversarial review by 3 reviewers every round (doc-aware invariant destroyer · cross-family blind destroyer · concurrency/teardown lens). The core defect was caught in round 1 — the partition key was the AgentId that rang the doorbell, not the actual injection target. **★This is not "passed in 3 rounds" (the authority for per-round coverage = this line)★** — round 3 was doc-aware PASS · blind 2 FIX, and those 2 (one being the scope of decision 3's `caller_inject_error`) were fixed in a 4th coder round with no review. That gap was caught by the ADR document review (5 FIX — decision 1/2 of the rejection grounds flipped · a counterexample to an invariant sentence · this overstatement · 0 lines of the `// ADR-0142` anchor · missing bidirectional link for ADR-0125), and closed by the 5th (anchor and wording) + a combined follow-up review of the 4th and 5th.
- **QA:** `/qa full` — build · workspace regression 38 targets 1312 cases · fmt · 5 isolation gates · tsc · frontend 647 cases · 2 measurements.
- **Measurement (method and result):** We parked the mail first, then spawned a Raw recipient and a StreamJson recipient in succession so the two doorbells overlapped, and compared the daemon debug log timestamps. From doorbell to delivery the Raw recipient took 501ms (pacing window), the JSON recipient under 1ms, and the JSON side finished 265ms and 383ms before Raw. Performed connected directly to the daemon — another worktree's app held the single-instance slot, so the app UI could not be measured.
- **New finding (not created by this change, registered as a separate tracking item):** mail delivered to a freshly spawned terminal recipient is not submitted — the CR arrives at about 0.5 seconds after spawn, but that session's claude finishes booting about 0.5 seconds later.

## S20.10 delivery segment started — fixed the targeting method as a decision (ADR-0154) and made the registry reach the owner (2026-08-18, `wt2`, mixed conversation → autonomous) · 2 commits (docs · code) · `/review code deep` 3 lenses × 3 rounds · `/review doc full` 4 rounds · `/qa full` **PARTIAL** (GUI measurement not run)

- **★The blockage was a misdiagnosis — the daemon starts normally★.** The previous handoff raised 「측정 환경에서 데몬이 안 뜬다」 as the next session's prerequisite task, but the measurement showed **the causation was wrong.**
  - The origin of `Origin header is not a valid URL` is **Tauri itself** (`tauri-2.11.3/src/ipc/protocol.rs:496` — failing while parsing the invoke request's `Origin` as a URL). That is, invoke **never even reached** Rust and is unrelated to the daemon. The previous session's observation that our net crate does not contain that phrase was right, but failing to find **where it came from** was the cause of the misdiagnosis.
  - **The lever was wrong too** — `daemon_ensure` by design never spawns (ADR-0021). This time that call behaved normally and returned `daemon down — connect 필요`. The spawn levers are `daemon_connect` and `daemon_start`.
  - When we launched a new app the daemon spawned and connected normally, and we **confirmed the registration of 15 shell commands from the log on a live socket** (the unverified item pointed to by the ★GUI measurement PARTIAL★ entry of the previous handoff is resolved by this).
- **★The app exited on its own twice — cause not identified★.** 8/17 01:17:38 and 01:20:41, both via the `tray quit_app` path. That path has only the tray menu 「완전 종료」 and `invoke('quit_app')`, yet the frontend has 0 occurrences of the `quit` string and nobody clicked. **A reproduction attempt left untouched for about 200 seconds did not die** — that is not evidence of 「원인 없음」 but only as far as 「짧은 창에서 안 났다」 (the two occurrences were 95 seconds and 27 minutes after startup).
- **★The delivery segment was not an enumerated item of TRD Step 3★** — all 5 details of §6 Step 3 are complete, and this gap existed nowhere in the enumeration but only as a placeholder comment in `connection_core.rs`. This is **the fourth 「열거에서 빠진 칸」 we met** (the previous three = the missing record of slice 5b · the 2 relay-envelope variants · S20.9's discovery of the delivery segment itself).
- **★Delivery is not a new implementation but a job of connecting what exists — the 3 stages are already in the tool crate and the shell uses it in production★.** `route()` (`OwnerLookup::Available(owner) => link.send(...)`) is the path the shell's `InboundCommands::on_command` actually runs. What is 0 is the **daemon call**, and the daemon never calls `route` at all. ★Once during the session it was mistranscribed as 「명부 조회는 테스트에서만 불린다」, and a worker refuted it★ — that misreading had inflated the unit size by 3 times.
- **★Decision — the daemon owns the targeting means (ADR-0154). ADR-0081 partially superseded.★** We put three branches (the daemon's own table / adding unicast to net / broadcast + recipient filter) up with their costs, and the user picked the first.
  - **What is discarded is not the premise but the one conclusion drawn from it** — ADR-0081's 「단일 앱 인스턴스 전제」 itself is alive (that premise **is true**: however many windows, the daemon has 1 connection — `src-tauri/src/daemon_client/mod.rs:3-4`, ADR-0036), and what dies is only **「대상 주소지정 불요」** derived from it. So **we did not touch TRD §1's v1 scope (multiple app instances as a non-goal).**
  - **The grounds for needing targeting are not the connection count** — stage 2 of the 3-stage delivery in ADR-0155 decision 3 is exactly 「주인 쪽 연결로 `link.send`」 (`trd.md:329`), and the same decision's Rejected alternative G rejected 2-stage routing on 「보낼 곳이 하나뿐이라는 전제」 (`:332`). ★Once during the session we used 「셸+웹+CLI가 같이 붙어 이질적이다」 as grounds and the review refuted it★ — **the CLI is not a WS peer but the HTTP control plane** (ADR-0132) and the web client is not used in production (`clientFactory.ts` swaps in `TauriTransport`). The only remaining measured ground is dev · release shell coexistence (`step-log.md:1794` ㊅).
  - **We do not change the net crate boundary — that it need not be changed is the measurement.** The crate that owns the send abstraction (`OutboundSink`) is not net but the **daemon**, and the connection's frame-send handle comes into the daemon's hands at `on_connect`. However, that argument is a **borrowed reference**, so it cannot be stored as is and the `Arc` must be cloned (`frame_port.rs` states 「빌린 참조로는 이 연결보다 오래 사는 sink를 못 만든다」 explicitly).
- **Implementation — the registry hands out that connection's frame outlet by owner token** (centered on `crates/engram-dashboard-daemon/src/command_roster.rs`, 4 files). The delivery itself, the request-correlation table, and the deadline are **outside this unit**.
  - `Shared.live` went from `BTreeSet<ConnId>` → `BTreeMap<ConnId, LiveConn>` and `LiveConn` holds **the owner token and the frame outlet together**. Being under **one lock** with the registry, `attach`/`detach` touch both fields atomically — so the **order of putting in and taking out creates no observable window** (the order itself was kept in the code as a defense).
  - **★The derivation point narrowed to `attach` alone★** — `detach` · `register` · `update`, and even the **client-claim comparison**, read the stored value. If compared against the derived value, on the day the storage leaves the derivation **an honest client gets caught and impersonation passes** (that comparison is log-only so it does not affect authorization). As a side effect `ConnectionSession::owner_token` now has **0 production consumers**.
  - **We do not parse the prefix string (`conn-<id>`) to trace back** — that derivation is something whose own comment stamped 「오늘의 잠정 규칙, 슬라이스 B가 대체한다」, so routing must not lean on its reversibility.
  - **We explicitly took on two costs of holding a strong handle:** drop the last strong reference **outside the lock** (the table does not know what the destructor does) · **do not hold the handed-out copy across a round trip** (there is no means of reclaiming it, so it is blocked only by the caller contract).
- **★The answer for the torn window = `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. But this is a chosen value, not a measured one★.** The race where the path disappears after the lookup answered `Available` remains even with one lock — because `route` releases the lock between lookup and delivery, and there is a test pinning that property (`the_roster_is_not_held_while_the_link_is_in_flight`).
  - The grounds for the choice = **retrying with the same id is safe and useful** (the owner can reattach). `UNKNOWN_COMMAND` is excluded as false certainty, and `OWNER_UNAVAILABLE` is unreachable after edition 3 so we do not revive it.
  - **★We closed the unconfirmed line of TRD §9 with this — not 「실측으로」 but 「결정으로」★.** During the session we stamped both documents saying it was closed by measurement, and the review refuted it and we reverted: what that unconfirmed item asked was **what the daemon delivery segment emits**, but that segment is 0 lines, so **there was nothing to measure.** What we measured was the vocabulary of `route`'s delivery branches, and those two spots are the **opposite condition** 「봉투가 이미 선을 탔을 수 있는」 and so cannot lend authority. We also recorded at that spot that 「이 경합이 `OWNER_UNAVAILABLE`의 자연스러운 미래 소유자」 in §4-⑦ was taken over by this decision.
- **Verification:** `/qa full` **all PASS**. 17 gates + ts-rs bindings sync (full workspace regression 0 failures · 2 shell integration targets 41+23 · all isolation gates · frontend 647) **+ GUI measurement**.
  - **GUI measurement was postponed once and filled in the next day** — at first another worktree's (wt3) session app held the single-instance lock so this worktree's app could not start (we did not terminate it since it was someone else's process). We ran it after that session ended. ★In between, the commit was labeled 「PARTIAL·push 금지」 and this line resolves that★ — that phrase in the `3eda93d` message is stale from this point on.
  - **What was measured = lifetime smoke** (the new table has 0 production consumers so there is no feature to show on screen): launch → daemon connect and authentication → **15 shell commands registered** (independently confirmed in both the shell and daemon logs) → window render → cleanup at exit.
  - ★**The decisive evidence is the disconnect log**★ — `연결 끊김 — 명령 명부에서 이 주인의 이름을 지웠다 conn=1 names=15`. It means **15 were actually found and erased by the stored owner token**, and had the token lookup broken, `removed` would have been empty and 「내릴 이름이 없다」 (`debug!`) would have shown up in its place. On the real connection `등록 패킷의 주인 토큰은 쓰지 않는다 claimed=engram-dashboard-shell` was also printed, so the behavior of this decision itself was observed.
  - **★1 procedure deviation (recorded)★** — the daemon file log defaults to `warn`, and **the daemon that discovery launches via WMI does not inherit the parent's `RUST_LOG`.** So in the first pass where only the app was launched with debug, the daemon log was a single header line and the `info!` line above was never recorded at all. A runtime level-change function exists but has **0 wire callers**, so it could not be raised while running either. We filled it by **launching the daemon first** as a detached run and passing the level (the branch CLAUDE.md specifies).
- **Review:** code = 3 lenses (invariant breaker · other-family blind · concurrency and lifetime) × 3 rounds → at the end the other-family **PASS** (8 axes clean), invariant lens FIX (document and test layer, unrelated to the gate). Docs = 4 rounds (BLOCK → BLOCK → FIX → FIX). **4 coder re-fixes, and before each round all findings were closed, so the loop cap was not reached.**
  - **★Mutation testing confirmed the tests bite★** — we reverted the implementation to the old way (re-derivation), saw the 3 new tests fail 3 of 3, and restored it.
  - **★3 things the main session got wrong (all caught by review)★:** ① the overstatement 「실측이었다」 (the scope differed) ② approving a debug assertion — at the very spot where 「여기서 패닉하면 정리 훅과 등록 해제를 건너뛴다」 is stated, so replaced with `tracing::error!` ③ the misreading 「명부 조회는 테스트에서만」.

**[S20.10 accrual 2026-08-18 — what we did not fix in this round. ★The numbers are valid only within this block★]**

- **★㊀ The certainty rule splits within the same file — user decision needed★.** `handler_panicked` in `route.rs` folds 「봉투가 나간 적이 없다」 into a **certain failure** (`ErrorCode::Internal`), while ADR-0154 folded a race with **the same condition description** into `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. This decision did not settle whether to unify the certainty rules of the two spots. **We did not invent a distinguishing reason** — both the reviewer and the main session refused fabrication.
- **㊁ No test catches a revert of the client-claim comparison.** The decision function itself is bitten by the 3 new tests, but **a change that reverts the call site to pass the derived value instead of `attached_owner`** breaks nowhere in the repository (there is no means to create a 「저장≠파생」 state at that layer — the table is private to another module). Without a `#[cfg(test)]` seam, signature pressure and the comment are all there is.
- **㊂ The owner lookup is a linear scan that runs while holding the lock, and the connection count has no cap.** If it runs once per delivery it contends for the same lock as registration and connection cleanup. We wrote the cost in the code and left the data structure as is — an inverted index or a connection cap is outside this unit.
- **㊃ Which connection to send to when one owner has several connections is undecided.** The value that comes out today is a by-product of the table iteration order, not a policy, and we **withdrew** the 「최소 연결 id」 promise. It becomes reachable the moment slice B changes the owner key (revisit trigger ②).
- **㊄ The new `error!` prints the owner token without sanitizing.** Today it is the daemon-made `conn-<id>` so it is harmless and that line itself is unreachable, but once slice B stores a client-authored identifier it becomes a spot that prints an unverified counterpart string raw. The sanitizer is private to another module so the wiring is not one line, and we only recorded it as debt.
- **★㊇ What we saw in GUI measurement — a connection opens twice on the daemon spawn path★.** Two connection-start lines appeared in the same microsecond and the WS generation split into 1 and 2. The earlier generation, after receiving up to Hello, is discarded as 「세대가 밀림」 — since the client filters by generation it is not a functional defect. **However, on the daemon side one more connection to be discarded gets attached.** In the pass where the daemon was launched in advance there was only one generation, so it looks like **a race that occurs only on the spawn path**. ★We could not observe how the daemon handled that discarded connection★ (the daemon in that pass was at `warn` level) — left as unverified.
- **★㊈ The daemon log level cannot be raised while running★.** The daemon file-log default is `warn`, and the path that discovery launches via WMI **does not inherit the parent's `RUST_LOG`.** A runtime level-change function exists but has **0 wire callers**. So a measurement that needs the daemon log must **launch the daemon in advance as a detached run** and pass the level — if only the app is launched with debug, the daemon log is a single header line. We learned this after this measurement ran idle once.
- **㊅ Pre-existing flake — a test that measures logs loses to thread order.** tracing **globally caches** callsite interest, so if a thread without a subscriber hits that spot first, a test that later measures that line comes away empty-handed. There are already 5 tests that hit that spot bare, and this addition wrapped it to make the incremental amount 0. If `a_detach_logs_the_names_it_removed` turns red, it is this mechanism, not a regression.

## S22 — integrate 2 fixes not yet in master + branch name cleanup (2026-08-18, `v0.2.0/chore/misc`, conversation session) · merges `d6af0a5` · `ce4abb6` · CI green · measurement PASS 2 items

- **Origin:** The user reported 「재spawn 후 모니터링하면 대기 인디케이터가 무한정 뜬다 — 분명히 고쳤는데?」. On investigation, **it was not that the push had not happened but that it had not been merged to master**. The fix commit `59b0e15` was riding on `v0.2.0/feat/command-bus` (the wt2 standing work branch), which has a different topic — a remnant of the old "branch = worktree name" convention, where whatever was done in that worktree piled onto that branch regardless of topic.
- **What ① (Wait stuck):** cherry-picked only the single commit `59b0e15` into `v0.2.0/fix/resume-wait-stuck` (new SHA `5883989`) → master. We did not merge the command bus body with it since it is incomplete. 1 file (`crates/engram-dashboard-core/src/agent/backend/claude.rs`, +63/-3).
- **What ② (dev/distribution concurrent-run regression):** moved the 12 files (+617/-26) of work left in the main worktree **not even committed** to `v0.2.0/fix/dev-identifier-regression`, committed → master. The second regression of ADR-0137 — the launcher bypassed the tauri CLI wrapper with a raw `cargo build`, so the release identifier was stamped on the debug exe again, and when the distribution was running the dev app died instantly without a window. Created `scripts/build-client-shell.mjs` (the single endpoint for build + identifier check) and `scripts/dev-config-json.mjs`, replaced both launchers and qa binding §full entirely to go through it, blocked the env leak channel of `tauri-cli.mjs`, fixed 2 concurrent-run defects of `launch-detached.ps1` (log filename collision · process misidentification by image name), and created 2 tests.
- **qa binding conflict resolution:** `.claude/skill-bindings/qa.md` §full diverged on both sides. Since **each fixed a different measurement incident**, we merged rather than picking one side — 4 places from the branch side (going through the build script · exe path measurement · path-based process decision · per-run log tag), 2 places from the master side (1420 owner check · dev server teardown clause).
- **Gates:** local `cargo test -p engram-dashboard-core` 372 PASS · `cargo fmt --check` OK · `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 · `npm test` 678 PASS. The 2 branches + master all **CI green**.
- **Measurement:** ① concurrent run — with the distribution (wt3 release) running, launched the debug app (main worktree) detached → both coexist, CDP 200 · 2 pages rendered. **Performed on the pre-merge branch state (`0a20e6f`)** and not re-measured on the final master (the absorbed part is frontend so unrelated to the identifier path). ② Wait stuck — **the user confirmed with the latest master build, resolved PASS** (2026-08-18).

- **What ③ (empty state):** mascot + "Claude Code" + a rounded input box in the center. ★The decision criterion is not "0 items" but "restore complete + 0 items + not yet sent"★ — the chat view empties the list at mount and history fills in asynchronously, so looking at 0 items alone makes the guidance appear and vanish in a session that has history. The restore-complete signal **had already reached the client as the 4th argument of `subscribeOutput` and nobody consumed it** (the terminal slot did not use it either — there an empty screen is natural so the problem was not visible). User decision = **the criterion is "the targeted agent does not exist right now" (death and connection loss the same), the screen is frozen as it looked at that moment, the whole thing is dimmed + one symbol in the center, no text.** ADR-0148. Connection loss is also included without wiring (only reads `agentClient.connectionState`).

Re-measuring in the running app, **the computed value of the `px-6` element was 0px**. Since preflight already makes the same declaration in `@layer base`, we **deleted** the block (ADR-0147). The user's remark (「툭 사라지는데 그게 기본 동작 아니냐」) + the debt that the threshold is recomputed every time the grid size changes (it was pushed back twice during the work). The height observation device · constant · branch · debounce were deleted wholesale.

Final = 26×17 grid based on the official sticker shape, color `#c97b5c`, **SVG merged render (DOM nodes 442→37)**.
- **Gates:** `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 · `npm test` 45 files **700 PASS**. `/review code full` 2 rounds — round 1 FIX 8 (restore display latch · awaiting contamination · center alignment error · missing resize debounce and others), round 2 FIX 8 (ADR rationale error · comment mismatch · 3 send races · slot-switch afterimage · missing regression gate), all applied. The coder also performed mutation verification (whether the corresponding test fails when the guard is removed).
