## S20.12 daemon own-table promotion + `agent.new` argumentization · pop-out into the shell table (2026-08-19, `wt2`, mixed conversation → autonomous) · commits `2f8d8f2` · `78dda08` · `/review code deep` 5 rounds + 1 independent re-derivation · `/qa full` **PASS** (including GUI measurement) · **rounds 2~5 were single-family — no cross-family cross-verification**

- **Delivery stage 1 (the daemon's own table) filled — lookup 15 → 20.** We resolved without bypassing the two things the code itself had written down as "reasons for not plugging in": the blocking contract where the handler writes to disk while holding the profile lock (→ open the seat first and race it against `spawn_blocking`) · the bypass of the entrance argument check (→ the two entrances share one `call_daemon_command`). `agent.{list,spawn,new,rename,move}` were raised onto the bus.
- **`agent.new` runs with arguments alone without a folder window.** cwd **or** preset, either one · screen mode (`Terminal`|`StreamJson`) · backend (closed vocabulary, currently only `Claude`). The backend is **placing the seat first**, and widening it is not additive — `AgentCommand` is serialized into `agents.json` as a tag so an old build cannot read the whole file. We wrote that fact in the declaration doc.
- **Pop-out (`slot.popout`) became the 16th of the shell table.** The instruction was "hook it onto the existing apply service" but **that service had no function** — two-phase commit · rollback · 「여전히 우리 것인가」 check · orphan prevention were all entangled with Tauri types in the `#[tauri::command]` body, so we moved them to `layout/apply.rs` and left only a thin wrapper. Two reviewers compared sentence by sentence and confirmed **identical behavior** down to six early returns · MOVE→COPY downgrade · event emission order · the frontend contract.
- **★The re-execution prevention device ate most of this unit — 5 review rounds★.** Since execution cannot be stopped even past the deadline (10 seconds) (`spawn_blocking` has no cancellation), only the answer is sent out at the deadline and the seat keeps holding the number. Fixing it each round produced something new: ① the deadline is ineffective so the frame does not go out and the re-query executes the write twice · side effects to a caller who has left ② a forged answer via a 「결말」 sent from outside · success after the deadline unrecorded ③ remembering 「이미 돌렸다」 when it did not run · read traffic pushing out write protection · the sizing rationale wrong ④ cleanup erasing the held seat of a dropped connection, so duplicates recur.
  - **★The convergence was made by independent re-derivation★** — a designer given only the problem without seeing the implementation rejected a separate completion list, saying **"the owner of the number space is the seat table alone. If one name space has two owners, they will diverge someday"**. When we removed that list, the three under ③ above vanished at once. The overall approach (only the answer at the deadline · execution continues · the number held) **converged the same way** as the independent design — the direction was right and the only place it diverged was exactly there.
  - **We flipped the decision to an allowlist of 「확실히 아무것도 안 했다」** — only `INVALID_ARGUMENT` · `NOT_FOUND` · `CONFLICT` are released and the rest are held. The opposite direction, enumerating 「적용됐을 수 있다」 by code, fails **open** on new verbs and reused codes. Over-holding blocks one retry inside the window, and under-holding leaves **a duplicate that cannot be erased** (`agent.new` has no delete verb).
  - **We read to confirm the premise** — the coder read the five verbs directly and found that only `agent.spawn` can 「만들어 놓고 실패」, and pinned that premise itself with a core test.
- **We confirmed every round that the tests actually bite.** The pop-out rollback test was counting **window count** so it stayed green even if the rollback body was deleted wholesale — switching the scale to View count made three collapse, and deleting only the resync makes one collapse separately. The `is_open` test also used a label present in neither the model nor the OS, so it was the model re-verification that blocked, not that port.
- **GUI measurement (both real app · real daemon):** confirmed lookup 20 → **registration with 0 folder windows** → confirmed in the list and screen → delete cleanup. Pop-out creates **a real OS window on both paths, bus and frontend**, the empty-area refusal wording is identical, and closing the window leaves 0 orphans in the model.
- **★4 items awaiting user decision — all are wire contracts so we did not settle them arbitrarily★:**
  - **Argument check on the bus path.** The code checks now, but the tool crate sentence and ADR-0157 wrote **categorically** 「배선은 검문하지 않는다 — 하면 앞선 버전 호출자가 옛 주인을 하드 실패시켜 additive 진화가 죽는다」. Reviewer verdict: it kept the letter of the rule but produced exactly the result that sentence tried to prevent, and in fact the bus frame path is **both a surface that an LLM hits and inter-hop wiring**, so ADR-0157's dichotomy does not cover this case.
  - **Changing a required argument of `agent.new` to optional.** A judgment made because 「둘 중 하나」 cannot be expressed in a schema, and the reviewer also saw the shape itself as right, but it directly hits the TRD §4-③ 「하면 안 되는 것」 table. That new contract currently lives in **the declaration doc comment and the test assertions** — the `cwd` field in `crates/engram-dashboard-core/src/agent/commands.rs` itself carries 「`preset` 과 상호배타 · 둘 중 정확히 하나」, and `crates/engram-dashboard-core/tests/command_declarations.rs` asserts 「`required` 가 비어 있는 것이 계약이고 조합 판정은 핸들러 몫」. **Where it is missing is the schema surface.** ★Correction (2026-08-22)★ This line had been recorded as 「테스트 주석에만 적혀 있다」 — a description that left out the declaration doc comment, and TRD §4-③ stamped that fact together as a revision mark.
  - **Registration rejection unit (whole packet vs per name)** — the reviewers split. Currently whole. Contract lens: when the shell in Step 4 also registers the screen's commands on its behalf, daemon-owned names get mixed in and **the packet containing all windows, tabs, and slots is rejected wholesale**. Invariant lens: it is a build-time property and the error wording explains itself, so it is not a runtime trap.
  - **Whether to keep carrying the re-execution prevention device.** It has value (preventing an unerasable duplicate) but ate most of the five rounds. If removed, instead of writing 「마감 후 재질의는 다시 실행될 수 있다」 as a known limit, the machinery vanishes entirely.

**[S20.12 accrual 2026-08-19 — what we wrote in code and deferred]**

- **㉵ The HTTP entrance (`/control/agent`) has no concurrency cap** — only the bus side is capped at 64. The shared point (`call_daemon_command`) is reached only after a pool thread is already held, so it cannot go there — a separate matter of threading admission through both `start_mcp_server` and `run_accept_loop` at assembly time. **Both reviewers named it priority 1 of the remaining items** (the only spot where real resource exhaustion is still possible).
- **㉶ When storage I/O gets stuck, its cap stays closed for the whole process lifetime** — `spawn_blocking` has no cancellation so a deadline cannot be set at this layer. The real deadline must live in the profile save path. It notifies every minute and the refusal wording points to a restart.
- **㉷ `LocalCommands::run` has no 「무엇을 적용했나」 channel** — so the hold decision infers from the error **code** (using the caller-advice channel as an application record). Currently it leans to the safe side and we documented `agent.new`'s `INTERNAL` over-holding, but **if any verb's error mapping changes in another crate, it silently diverges again.** The real fix = add an applied-signal to the port.
- **㉸ A machine cannot check whether the declared `effect` matches the handler's actual behavior** — if one wrongly declares `Read`, duplicate prevention vanishes with neither error nor log. We wrote at the reading spot the fact that the declaration became **a consistency input**, not an advertisement.
- **㉹ The lock is released once between the pop-out window check and the model mutation** — if the user closes the target window in that gap it **splits two ways and the new-window side is worse.** For an existing window, the late cleanup also erases the tab just inserted, so the model is clean but the content is on no screen; **for a new window, the cleanup meets a label not yet in the model and just passes, and nothing cleans up afterward**, so a window and tab with no screen remain permanently (no recovery path other than `window.list` → `window.close`). The coordination method is a decision matter so we only corrected the comment to match the facts.
- **㉺ The bus path skips the frontend's render-mode cleanup** — `slot.close` · `slot.assignAgent` · `layout.setSlotContent` are the same class. It is the job of the step that promotes screen-owned state into commands.
- **㉻ The `engram agent new` CLI flags have no new arguments** — the bus and HTTP accept them but the CLI vocabulary is closed to `--cwd` · `--name` · `--parent`. **The catalog an LLM reads is the bus's**, so a caller who learned `preset` · `output_format` · `backend` from the catalog cannot hit them through the CLI.
- **⓪ The pop-out label is issued first even on a failed attempt** — the issuer runs before argument validation so the number skips (measured: 1 → 4). Not created by this change but an original property.

**[S20.12 documentation debt]** ADR not written — this unit's major decisions (the seat as the single owner of the number space · the allowlist direction of the hold decision · the answer field `new_view_id` divergence) are **only in the commit body and code comments**. ★Correction (2026-08-22)★ This line recorded that `docs/process/S20-command-bus/trd.md:713` still described `moveSlotToWindow` as 「command 로 승격 대기」 and thus conflicted with this change, but **TRD edition 4 closed that conflict** — the promotion-pending count in §6 Step 5 of the same document is now **five** and `moveSlotToWindow` dropped out as 「이미 덮였다」 (★do not pin line numbers — find it by section name★). The carry-over from the last session (`CLAUDE.md` shell integration targets 「두 줄」 → three · TRD §4-④) is likewise still not done.

## S20.13 entrance stage 1 — an agent looks at the registry and calls by name (2026-08-19, `wt2`, mixed conversation → autonomous) · commits `002a887` (daemon) · `da18d88` (CLI) · `/review code deep` 3 rounds each · `/qa standard` **PASS** · **rounds 2~3 were single-family — no cross-family cross-verification**

- **What the problem was:** An agent launched by the dashboard holds a single `engram` in its shell, but that CLI had only three addresses it could speak to on the daemon (send mail · read · the agent family) and **no way to ask what could be called.** The argument alphabet was also closed at build time, so even the registration arguments (preset · mode · backend) that S20.12 created could not be hit through the CLI.
- **Daemon half (`002a887`) — two addresses.** `POST /control/commands` (the whole registry, in name order, `help` as the bytes the owner registered, verbatim) · `POST /control/call` (execute by full name). We used the existing `call_daemon_command` (check existence → argument check → execute) as is, so we did not create a second unchecked entrance. Authentication is applied across the whole router so **the new addresses inherit it for free** (we did not assume it; we confirmed 401 over real HTTP with no token and with a wrong token).
  - **★We changed `available` to `callable`★** — At first we used the socket side's list type as is, but its `available` means 「주인이 붙어 있나」, which differs from the reachability of this entrance. A dashboard-owned name cannot be called through this entrance even when its owner is attached, yet it went out as `true` in the list — **a machine-read field said the opposite of the prose.** `callable` is the same fact the execution branch looks at (both one BTreeMap · the slot is `OnceLock`), and a name that cannot be called answers `UNSUPPORTED` so it is distinguished from 「모르는 이름」.
  - **We wrote the body parser by hand** — the default method also accepted a JSON **array** as positional arguments, so the single line `["agent.list"]` actually **executed a command.** A test measures that.
  - We wrapped `args` rather than flattening — one argument of `agent.rename` is literally named `name`, so flattening would collide with the command name and that verb could not be called.
  - We extracted the registry merge (daemon table + registered, daemon wins on overlap, name order) into one place so the socket and HTTP use the same function. If the two surfaces answer existence differently, discovery becomes false.
- **CLI half (`da18d88`) — the third surface.** If the first token has a dot it is a command name, otherwise the existing family parsing (unchanged). `engram commands` (name + one line, with a separate section stating that those that cannot be called are `UNSUPPORTED`) · `engram commands <이름>` (arguments · types · return · errors) · `engram <이름> --키 값` (execute).
  - **We do not guess argument types** — right before calling we receive the schema and match to the **declared type**. `--name 123` goes out as a string since that field is a string. Guessing from the value's shape silently goes wrong the moment a name or folder looks like a number.
  - **We preserved the property that `engram help` is static and answers without the daemon** (ADR-0132 decision 4) — we added just one line pointing to the new verbs.
- **★The heavy ones among what the review caught★:**
  - **`--help` could execute a write command** — only this surface did not know the help token, so for a command that declared a boolean argument named `help`, the help request was executed as is. The 1st fix blocked **only the first position** and it survived by changing position, and the 2nd closed it regardless of position.
  - **`agent.move` could not be called by full name** — detaching the parent is null, but the new path could not send null so the string `"none"` went out. We made it able to send null, but that word has a special meaning **only in a required ∧ nullable field** — at first we applied it to every nullable, so `--cwd none` went **silently to the default folder** (the reply does not reveal that fact).
  - **A newline in a registered name could create a fake line in the list** — names are checked only for length and nobody looks at character kinds. We filter every caller string printed to the screen through one gate and measure the alignment width with the filtered string too.
  - **One broken line killed the whole surface with exit 2** · **a list lookup failure looked like a command failure** (the LLM starts fixing perfectly good arguments) · **the success decision diverged from the old path** (the same command and same response gave exit 2 on the old path and 0 on the new).
- **★The ADR-0130 detector was broken★** — the command that guards 「`control/` 에서 나가는 간선 0」 had four sibling module names hardcoded, so **it had been unable to see the edge created in the first step of S20 ever since.** This time a second appeared and it still reported 0 lines. We fixed it to extract the module list from the declarations and it now catches three (the two test fixtures are behind the boundary so they are filtered by the existing rule). **We did not touch the decision, the Rejected alternatives, or the status — only the tool was fixed.** Resumption condition ② has actually fired, and its revisit awaits the user's decision.
- **Verification:** daemon 15 targets 0 failures (unit 115 · CLI process 43 · `control_agent` 33 · `mail_gate` 7) · workspace 0 failures · frontend 722 · tsc · fmt · core isolation · shell integration 49+27+4 · generated drift 0. CI green twice. **For each heavy fix we reverted and confirmed the test actually turns red.**
- **User decisions (this session):** work order = entrance first · CLI call form = full name without the family (`engram slot.split …`) · list = `engram commands`, top level is name + one line and details separate · **deriving help from the registry is a follow-up after the command bus is done** (static for now).

**[S20.13 accrual 2026-08-19 — what the review caught and we did not fix this time]**

- **㊀ The mail block hangs on the address, but the execution address calls by the name in the body.** Today the daemon table has only `agent.*` so it does not fire, but `control/commands.rs` already wrote 「우편 명령이 이 표로 들어올 예정」 and on that day **a blocked credential calls `mail.send` by full name.** The address is a closed enum so the compiler enforces it, but **the command set behind that address is not.** Two reviewers pointed it out. We left only the fact as a comment at the classification spot. Handling = change the gate to key on the command being called (touches the invariant of an existing decision) or do not bring mail commands into that table.
- **㊁ The list lookup shares the registry lock with delivery.** `entries()` copies the whole registry **while holding the lock**, and that lock is also used by delivery and connection cleanup. We moved it down to the blocking pool so **who waits changed, but the lock hold time is the same** — any agent repeating lookups pushes delivery back (cap 4096×4KB ≈ 16MB). Coder proposal = put a revision number on the registry and keep an `Arc` snapshot rebuilt only on change, with the reader copying just that one `Arc`.
- **㊂ These two addresses are in no decision record** — neither `/control/commands` nor `/control/call` is in the TRD or ADRs. Moreover, the existing decision on discovery method (ADR-0132 decision 4) chose **static help** but this time a second discovery surface, the **runtime list**, arose. It is heavier because it is not 「미작성」 but a matter where **directions diverge**.
- **㊃ A name without a dot shows up in the list but cannot be called** — nobody enforces the rule that a name must have a dot (registration checks only the 128-byte length). Whether to put a name rule on the producer side is a decision matter.
- **㊄ If a declared return is not an object, the screen and the decision diverge** — the screen honestly says 「배열」 and the decision gives exit 2. No such command exists yet.
- **㊅ The success decision looks only at 「칸이 있나」** — it passes if the value is an explicit `null`, but the old path rejects if empty. For the same command a state remains where **the old entrance is stricter**.
- **㊆ The caller-string gate does not block format characters** — zero-width characters and RTL reversal can make a name look different to human eyes (lookup is exact match so no hijack, only confusion). A whitespace-only name renders as a line with only a summary.
- **㊇ There is no `engram help commands` screen**, and the top-level usage line still explains only the two-token form. The 「모르는 명령」 guidance points to a list that can never contain `mail.*`.
- **㊈ A boolean cannot be given to a command with no schema** (putting `true` into a valueless flag is a guess this surface forbids, so we left it documented) · exotic schema shapes (`$ref` · `oneOf` · `allOf` · non-string enum) go out as strings.

## S20.14 subscription zombie 3-layer closure + resend dimensions on reattach — the screen reattaches even when the daemon is swapped (2026-08-20~21, `wt2`, conversation) · commits `db8197a` · `156a2ff` · `788051b` + 4 documents (`75dd65b` · `bf1e6d6` · `16f0358` · `7a2a223`) + handoff `efe3517` · 1 document reviewer (reference implementation record) · all gates + **GUI measurement PASS (reproduced twice)** · **21 uncommitted files this session** (18 modified + 3 new ADRs — the 「이번 세션」 section below)

- **Subscription zombie, 3 layers (`db8197a`).** ① **A rejected subscription held a seat forever** — the rejection is now signaled on the wire and the shell releases the replay seat. ② **We changed generation identity from a sequential counter to a random marker drawn per generation** — not persisted, only compared for same/different. So a freshly launched daemon **structurally** differs from the previous one (a sequential number returns to the same value on restart). ③ We moved **the subscription trigger** from 「소켓이 붙었나」 to 「그 에이전트가 권위 명부에 있나」, and moved the screen clearing from request time to **replay arrival time**.
  - **Side fix — storage format asymmetry.** The generation value is **ignored on read but written as 0.** Without this, an old build could not parse a registry file written by this build, would push it aside as `.corrupt`, and **come up with an empty registry** — profiles, session ids, and the tree would vanish wholesale.
- **Resend terminal dimensions on reattach (`156a2ff`) — a regression `db8197a` caused.** A restored PTY comes up at the default 80×24 but the real screen grid differs (measured 137×25). The claude TUI computes 「위로 N 줄 지우기」 with **the size it believes**, so **even a one-line mismatch leaves a stale copy line every frame** — this is the 「글자가 두 번 찍힌다」 the user saw. The **only path** that propagated the size on reattach broke the moment the generation marker was dropped from that effect's deps (a daemon restart changes neither the view nor the agent).
  - **★Do not fix it by putting the marker back into deps★** — that clears the screen **before** the replay arrives and destroys unrecoverable scrollback. The review once returned BLOCK on exactly that form. Fix = **fit on the reattach signal and then resend the size.** We left a warning comment in the code.
- **★`788051b` 「스크롤바 가시성 통일」 has no effect — do not trust the claim in the commit body★.** The rule **does not reach the screen**: xterm 6.0 draws the visible terminal scrollbar as a **DOM element** through the VS Code scroll component, so the `::-webkit-scrollbar` block in `src/index.css` is currently **dead code**. We forced the thumb color to red and proved it with **0** matching pixels in the full capture.
- **4 documentation and number items.** `bf1e6d6` terminal scrollbar thickness 14px → 6px, matched to the structured surface (pixel-measured — at dpr 1.5, 9 device px = 6 CSS px) · `16f0358` recorded in the reference implementations the locations of five local peer clones (herdr · wezterm · zellij · ttyd · orca) and what each is a peer of, passed a 1-reviewer document review + corrected 3 factual errors through that review · `75dd65b` created the debt list (`docs/backlog.md`) · `efe3517` handoff.
- **Scrollbar direction (B) settled + the work volume split into 2 stages (`7a2a223`).** (B) = make xterm's own scrollbar **width 0 via a public option** and lay our thumb on top. Stage 1 = terminal only, stage 2 = app-wide unification. **★Going with (B) discards the thickness CSS that `bf1e6d6` added★** and making the width 0 **changes the terminal column count, so the size renegotiation falls inside stage 1.**
- **Verification (that session):** workspace regression 1703 passed · shell integration 4 targets (49/27/4/9) · fmt · isolation gates 4 · discovery async · generated sync · frontend 812 passed · tsc 0 · **GUI measurement PASS, reproduced twice** (spawn → banner → daemon kill → banner preserved + input blocked → new daemon → new-generation output arrived, all four generation markers differ from each other and are not sequential numbers). The user confirmed the dimension fix directly on screen.
- **★What was not verified (that session)★:** ① **We could not measure the final state where the restored agent survives and keeps showing the banner** — a session with no conversation by design always fails to resume, so what was confirmed is only up to 「새 세대의 출력이 슬롯에 닿는다」. ② Whether the thumb pixels are really redrawn in real scrollback — we measured only the computed transition and the marker toggle. ③ The fact that the `788051b` rule above does not reach the screen. ④ We did not check the thickness change across the theme set (color unchanged, the width token is theme-independent).

**[This session 2026-08-21 — 21 uncommitted files: 18 modified + 3 new ADRs · the `/review doc` adversarial review returned BLOCK, and the corrections in this entry respond to the findings 「이번 세션 자기 산출물에 걸린 분」 — the rest were not fixed and were accrued as debt (the list is under `docs/backlog.md`'s jurisdiction)]**

## S20.15 UI settings file + `ui.refresh` pilot — swap the display policy from outside (2026-08-21, `wt2`, mixed conversation → autonomous) · commit `6bcda88` (code 12 files +1534/−21) · ADR-0166 new · `/implement standard` · `/review code full` **5 rounds** · `/qa full` **PASS** (including 4 GUI measurements)

- **What we built.** The shell reads `<data_dir>/ui-settings.json` (one key, `theme`) and applies it to the screen, and the command `ui.refresh` re-reads and reapplies it. The one who edits the file is an outside agent and the shell only reads. This is **the first piece of the direction of not creating a command per value**, and the decision and Rejected alternatives are owned by ADR-0166.
  - **Two read points** — boot is pulled by the frontend (`get_ui_settings`), and updates are pushed by the shell (`ui:settings-updated`). Both use the same payload struct, so **the reason field of the answer rode on both paths with 0 lines of wiring.**
  - **It was added as the 17th name of the shell table** — it rides the declaration, registration, and inbound path that Step 3 opened as is, so there is no new wiring. `catalog_version` 3 → 4 (the answer shape is also a declaration so it goes up), name count 17, `since` stays 3.
- **★This pilot is not Step 4★** — Step 4 is the path where **the shell registers the webview registry on its behalf** and is not yet started. This one is the shell declaring one more command of its own. Do not confuse it with the 「길만 뚫기」 direction (user decision 2026-08-21 — only the path instead of registering all 33).
- **4 user decisions (2026-08-21).** ① the file is the authority and the command is `ui.refresh` alone — no command per value ② **carry the reason in the answer** (the first implementation returned only `{theme}` and we reversed it — even when the agent made a typo a success response came back) ③ but **the reason goes only to two branches** — 「사유 때문에 로직 키우지 마라」 ④ the 3 reviewer conflicts were closed as **proceed as is** (below).
- **4 main-session decisions.** Ignore unknown keys (forward compatibility) · keep `error!` for parse failure (the explicit branch of the logging convention + a repository precedent) · file missing `warn!` → `debug!` (a new install is a normal state — the spot the convention cites passes `NotFound` quietly) · values to put in the log only those that **pass the shape gate**.
- **★The reason the review went 5 rounds is not a coder failure★** — consecutive unresolved **0** (we closed every finding each round). Each round the blind reviewer found **something new**, and round 4 was not a defect fix but the addition of a user-directed feature (the reason field). doc-aware was PASS in rounds 3, 4, 5 consecutively.
- **Mutation verification actually paid off.** **Two tests** written in round 1 were **spinning idle** — the child in the remount-prevention test subscribed to nothing so it passed regardless of the implementation, and the cap test stayed green even with `.take()` deleted. After that we required of every fix 「고친 것을 되돌리면 그 테스트만 실패하는가」 and it was confirmed each time. **The coder also made one real defect in their own test harness and caught it** (the mock reset cleared only the call records, so the 3 lifetime tests that followed ran wholesale in "a world where subscription always fails").
- **★The two reviewers split head-on and the user decided★** — doc-aware "PASS, ship it" vs blind "must-fix 3". Two of the three were **re-raises of already-made decisions** (an old notification overwriting a new value = doc-aware judged "not a defect" twice · a short-value log leak = a tradeoff the user chose), and one was new (a broadcast reaching 0 subscribers still answers success — the boot lookup overwrites the screen so the real harm is small). User decision = **proceed as is**, all three recorded as residue.
  - **There is a structural reason blind repeated the same thing for four rounds** — by design it does not receive the decision rationale so it does not know the decisions we made. And **the 3 noise items in rounds 2 and 3 arose because the contract summary I gave blind was wrong** ("exactly one key" · "record at warning level" — both differ from the actual project). After I corrected the summary that branch disappeared.
- **Verification (all measured in this session):** `cargo build` · workspace regression 0 failures · shell integration 4 targets (`layout_commands` 44 · `layout_apply` 49 · `daemon_client_pending` 4 · `daemon_client_replay` 9) · `npm test` 825 · `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 · `cargo fmt --check` · core isolation 0 lines · bindings sync gate PASS · **GUI measurement 4 kinds PASS** — boot with the saved theme (`light`) · on switching to `e-ink` via `ui.refresh`, DOM node count 41 identical (remount 0) · broken file → `dark` with no crash · file missing → `dark`. After measurement we cleaned up the app and daemon, and left the vite that was originally running untouched.
- **★What was not verified★:** ① **We could not measure the answer's reason field through the GUI** — the path that calls a bus command from the webview (webview → daemon → the same shell) did not return a response. It was a synthetic path that called a private method with a hand-made envelope so it is unclear whether it is a product defect, and the reason field itself is covered by unit tests with mutation verification. ② The real `app.emit` failure line is unverified residue (it needs a live `AppHandle` and cannot run in this package — QA cannot close it either) ③ There is no harness asserting the log level — it stays green even if `NotFound→debug` · parse→`error` · success→`debug` get swapped by a one-word edit.
- **We tightened the `/implement` re-fix hard cap from 5 to 3** (user decision 2026-08-21, outside this repository since it is a global skill file).
- **★Deferred — two sentences of `CLAUDE.md` 「프론트 구조」 became more wrong with this change★.** "The registering parties split into two" is actually **four** (`api/tauriTransport.ts` · `store/viewStore.ts` · `components/layout/WindowLayout.tsx` · this time's `theme/uiSettings.ts`), and "no direct calls to individual IPC helpers … there is no such module now" is refuted by `uiSettings.ts`. **This change did not create the drift (the first three already existed) but added one.** It is a load-bearing document so we did not touch it without `/review doc` — **we bundle it with the TRD drift in the Step 4 prerequisite document cleanup pass and review it once.**
- **Side work — re-deriving the S20 TRD drift.** We re-extracted what the earlier session wrote as "9 items" without leaving the list anywhere. **The result is more than 9 — the existing 12 + 3 created by this uncommitted work + 1 false completion claim in step-log.** ★The heaviest = **Step 3 is not finished**★ — step-log wrote "all 5 details complete", but the fifth (the client-authored identifier) is unimplemented, and since the daemon owner key is still derived from the connection id, on reconnect the registration is **stacking, not overwriting**. Step 4 stands on that token. Next is that **three things the document wrote as "does not exist today" already exist** (the shared apply service · the inbound receiver · the deadlock regression test) — a Step 4 coder reading this document would rebuild what already exists. **We fix this document before starting Step 4.**

## S20.17 Step 4 — open the path for screen commands to reach the daemon bus (2026-08-23, `wt2`) · commit `85aa6ab` · CI green (`941d1ad`) · review 3 rounds (final doc-aware PASS) · **GUI measurement PASS** · ★**an entry written after the fact**★

★**The number is late — the position is chronological**★ This entry landed before S20.16 (Step 5) (`85aa6ab` → `1dfab24` · `5b7b748`) but the record was omitted then, so it received its number later. **The sort axis of this file is time, not number** (at the top 「시간순 기록」 · numbers are originally interleaved as in S20.4→S21→S20.5, S20.11→S23→S20.12), so the position follows the landing order and only the number comes after.

- **What we opened.** What an agent could call was only the daemon's commands and the shell's commands, and **the daemon did not even know the names of the screen-side commands** a human clicks. We opened that path — window boot → report its own list to the shell → the shell merges it into its own registration packet and sends it up to the daemon → the daemon delivers that name → if it is not in the shell table, send it down to the screen → the screen executes and replies with the outcome. New = `src-tauri/src/view_commands.rs` · `src-tauri/src/commands/view_bus.rs` · `src/commands/viewCommandBridge.ts`.
- **★Not full registration — four for proof★** `theme.set` · `theme.toggle` · `tab.next` · `slot.empty`. Raising more is a matter of adding one description field to the declaration. ★**But nine cannot be raised**★ — 7 have names that **literally overlap** the shell declarations so even if registered they would never reach, and 2 collide with the daemon answering under its own name. ★If even one of the latter gets mixed in the daemon rejects the whole packet★ — so we **derive** the filtering net **from the declarations** (`reserved_names` in `view_commands.rs`). A hand list would silently go stale as the vocabulary grows and **the whole registration would die**.
- **The gate that decides boarding = a single `help` field.** We added `help` to `Command` in `src/commands/registry.ts` additively and `list()` returns it — `offeredCommands()` puts out **only those whose description (`help.summary`) is actually filled** (`viewCommandBridge.ts` — even with the field present, an empty string or whitespace drops out). ★**Where it diverged from the TRD plan**★ — in §6 Step 4 it was `help: string` (required) but the actual is `help?: CommandHelp` (**optional** · structured). That **optionality** became the boarding gate (we stamped it as a correction in that TRD section).
- **5 design decisions (the commit body is the authority).** ① the advertised set and the executing window come from **the same window** — reports are kept per window and only the owner window's is advertised (we do not build a contract on top of the coincidence that all windows report the same list today) ② the shell deadline fits **within the outer budget** (4s + 3s margin ≤ daemon 7s — if inverted the shell timeout becomes unreachable and the same command runs twice. A test that reads both real constants bites that inequality) ③ a reply may be made only by **the window that actually received that envelope** (checking against 「지금 주인」 rejects the real answer the moment the owner changes and lets a forgery from the old owner through) ④ **remove hidden windows** from the last-resort destinations (derived from settings — otherwise, when the main report fails, we paint an invisible window and the caller receives success) ⑤ the read/write marker is **carried from the screen declaration** (a required field — choosing a default is itself a lie so items without a marker are dropped from registration).
- **Verification (stated in the commit body):** workspace regression 0 failures · shell integration 4 kinds (63/49/4/9) · frontend 838 · `npx tsc --noEmit` · `cargo fmt --check` · core isolation 0 lines · bindings sync drift 0. **GUI measurement** — daemon list **21** (shell 17 + screen 4) · a bus call runs only in main and the tree window is unchanged · thrown from the tree window, main still executes · a report from a non-owner window leaves the advertisement unchanged.
  - ★**`CI 초록` is not in this commit body — the source is different**★ It is what the **title** of the handoff commit `941d1ad` says (that commit's body is only trailers), and `CI 초록(941d1ad)` in the title line above points to that source. Do not mix it into the 「커밋 본문 기재」 list.
- **★Three things not verified★:** ① **whether the hidden main stays in the window list** — the design stands on that premise, but the app permission blocks the automation's window hide and close so we could not measure it via GUI. We blocked the **outcome** instead of the premise (decision ④ above) ② **the differential-send success path** — all windows report the same set so no differential arises. Unverified until the set can diverge ③ **owner death** between lookup and delivery (the `UNSUPPORTED` branch) — there is no test that creates that interleaving.
- **★Of the four raised, the two themes were later withdrawn★** — ADR-0167 decision 5 (display state is settings-file data, not a command). Today the bus boarding list is two, `tab.next` · `slot.empty` (the same number as measurement ㉢ of S20.16).
- **The same commit fixed two documents.** TRD §7 — why 「선언마다 설명 검사」 does not stand and the replacement net (the list lock). `CLAUDE.md` 「프론트 구조」 — we replaced the sentence that **counted** the registering parties with a rule + a command to find them (the counting sentence was wrong twice in a row: it said two and was actually four). **What S20.15 wrote as 「Step 4 선행 문서 정리 패스로 미룬다」 was two, and only the 「등록 주체」 item was closed here** — the other one (`src/theme/uiSettings.ts` refutes 「개별 IPC 헬퍼 직접 호출 금지 … 그런 모듈은 지금 없다」) stays open as is and was moved to the backlog.

## S20.16 Step 5 — remove two side doors, control goes through the command table (2026-08-23, `wt2`) · commits `1dfab24` · `5b7b748` · CI green · **GUI measurement PASS** (release build) · **chat diverged from the TRD plan**

- **① Promote five render modes (`1dfab24`).** Created `src/commands/renderModeCommands.ts` — `slot.renderMode.set|clear` · `slot.domMode.enable|disable|toggle`. These are the last five reachable only through the side door, and are now caught in `__engramCmd.list()` and searchable from the palette (the side door had no list function so you had to remember the names). The argument is `{ slotId }` alone — which differs from the sibling `slot.*` `requireCoords` because the action does not use viewId and slotId is a window-global unique UUID. An invalid mode throws at the command layer instead of the store's warn-then-ignore (a warn does not reach a remote caller and it looks like `ok`).
  - ★**We do not put them on the bus**★ — we did not attach `help` and the gate that decides boarding is that one field (`offeredCommands` in `src/commands/viewCommandBridge.ts`). `renderModeOverride` is frontend state that is **per window** but the envelope goes only to the one host window the shell chose, and that host moves around during execution (ADR-0167). We stamped the warning in that file's header.
- **② Delete two handles (`5b7b748`).** In `src/store/eventBus.ts` we removed `window.__engramLayout` (15 methods) and `window.__engramChat` (5 items) and cleaned up about 23 comment spots. **Apart from the deletion itself there is no behavior change** — we did not touch the logic of the remaining code and the edits are definition removal and comments only. ★But the deletion itself is a behavior change★ — 20 callable global entries vanished and 5 of them, the chat ones, have no replacement path (the cost below). `rg "__engramLayout|__engramChat" src/ src-tauri/` → **0 lines**.
  - We **compared the 15 one by one against the registry** (10 had existed from the start and five are ①). Some are actually supersets — `window.close` may omit the label and `tab.close` may omit the view.
  - ★**Do not read it as 「전부 일대일 대체」 — there is one spot that narrowed**★ `moveSlotToWindow(slotId, toWindow?)` accepted a destination, but the frontend `slot.popout` has no destination argument so it is **always a new window**. That is, **moving a slot to an existing window is not reachable through `__engramCmd`** — the shell table has a `to_window` branch, but it is a transitional split state where what the two accept and give differ (memos pointing at each other are attached in both sources). Replacement = the invoke direct path below.
- **★None of the 5 chat items was promoted — the only spot that diverged from the TRD plan★** TRD §6 Step 5 said "promote all 5 items to commands → delete the handle" but the actual is **0 promoted · handle deleted only**. **That classification and the accepted cost are owned by ADR-0169** — not copied here.
- **Two costs accepted.**
  - **The narrowing of the reaching path is convenience, not capability.** With `withGlobalTauri` on (`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`), CDP still calls the shell directly via `window.__TAURI__.core.invoke('list_tabs', …)` and `invoke('move_slot_to_window', {viewId, slotId, toWindow})`. What is gone is **the path through the command table**.
  - ★**For now there is no means to change the chat style in a release build**★ — it is a live 「LLM-우선 제어」 gap so that section of `CLAUDE.md` cites it as current state. History and alternatives are in ADR-0169.

This time we tried to write that number by hand and **got it wrong twice** (the code comment said "two", actually three), so we **changed to a way to find them instead of a list**. Policy and current-state authority = `CLAUDE.md` 「LLM-우선 제어」.
- **Verification:** CI green · `npm test` 852 · `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 · **GUI measurement PASS** (`5b7b748` release build).
- **We ran the documentation sync the same day** (no code change, `/review doc full` 2 reviewers → FIX applied). **We do not write here which files were fixed** — that list is held by git, and copying it becomes false the moment a file moves.
  - **3 measurements that came out of that process.** ㉠ The shell lookup commands are **three, not four** — only `tab.list` · `window.list` · `slot.resolveSpatial` stand, and `get_view` has a recursive return type so the declaration macro cannot carry it (authority = the header of `src-tauri/src/layout/commands.rs`). ㉡ The registered commands in `src/commands/` are **36** (34 literal ids + 2 `registerSplit`) — the documents had gone stale twice at 33 and 31, and **we decided to stop updating that number by hand** (the registry enumerates itself through `__engramCmd.list()`). ㉢ **The bus boarding list is still two** (`ON_THE_BUS` = `tab.next` · `slot.empty`) — a different axis from the registered count.

## S24 frame visual cleanup — font · tabs · tree icons · borders (2026-08-23, `v0.2.0/refactor/frame-visual`, conversation session) · ADR-0168 new (partial amendment of 0066 · 0062 · 0075) · `/review code full` 2 adversarial + 1 additional blind · GUI measurement PASS (3-theme color comparison)

- **What we did.** We compared the screen with a mature peer (orca), narrowed the source of the "hand-made look" to the frame, and fixed it. We did not touch the *inside* of the slots (chat · terminal · diff). The decisions and Rejected alternatives are owned by ADR-0168.
  - **The font was priority 1 in perceived impact** — `--font-ui` was `'JetBrains Mono', monospace` but ★that font was not installed in this environment★. There is no `@font-face` at all so it depends only on system installation, and in practice it was being drawn with a generic monospace fallback. That is, **the intended font was never once applied.** `Inter` (`--font-claude-prose`) is the same. Replaced with the Windows built-in stack (Segoe UI Variable Text → Segoe UI → Malgun Gothic).
  - Tabs = Chrome layout (the active one is brighter than the bar · separators only between inactive ones · `×` always shown) · tree status glyph characters → lucide icons · rows 24→28px · border tone down · header underline removed · focus ring 65→40%.
  - **We connected the allotment divider that had been cut off from the theme** — the library default CSS's `--separator-border` (a gray literal) and `--focus-border` (VS Code `#007fd4`) were hardcoded in `:root` and did not follow theme switching. We override with `html:root` (0,1,1) — because allotment comes later in the bundle and would lose by order.
- **★The review brought out three defects that screen comparison cannot catch★.** All three are regressions this session *created*.
  - **The tree selection indicator vanished entirely in light · e-ink** — we chose `--surface-elevated` for the selection background, but that value is light (`#ffffff`) · e-ink (`#f0f0f0`), which is **the same as** the panel background `--bg-secondary` (`#fff` · `#f0f0f0`). Only dark differs so the eye did not catch it. Replaced with `color-mix(--text 12%, --bg-secondary)` — since `--text` by definition contrasts with the background, it separates in all three themes.
  - **The invisible close `×` received keyboard focus** — we made it visible only on hover with `opacity: 0` alone, but that turns off only painting and leaves hit-test and tab order as is. Reaching it with the Tab key and pressing Enter **closed something with no indication on screen of what was closing**. On the user's judgment we removed the hover fade itself (a close button simply being visible is normal).
  - **The icons vanished from the accessibility tree** — lucide automatically attaches `aria-hidden` to the svg when there is no accessibility prop. The role that `textContent` played in the text-glyph days became an empty string, so a Running row and an Exited row read identically. Restored with `role="img" + aria-label`.
- **★Two changes I instructed were reversals of already-made user decisions and the coder stopped them★** — focus ring 40% (a value ADR-0066 **explicitly rejected**) and the `+` icon 44→24px (ADR-0143 nailed it as "larger than 32px" and a regression test guards it). The cause is that I wrote the spec without looking at the ADRs. The former the user re-decided through a real-screen 3-step comparison (65→50→40) and we amended it in ADR-0168; the latter was withdrawn.
- **The tab layout changed four times (all decided on the real screen).** Original → bar bright and active dark → bar with `--text` 25% blended → reverted → Chrome layout. The reasons for the two discarded are in ADR-0168 「거부한 대안」 — the gray band played apart from the tree panel, and active tab = `--bg` became the darkest in the frame and read like a hole.
- **★We had to move branches★** — the `v0.2.0/chore/misc` we were working on was **12 commits behind** master, and in between the per-window theme feature (ADR-0166/0167) had come in. That is, the "813 passed" report was a pass in a state without that feature. We cut a new branch from master and moved to worktree `wt1` and re-verified — all 10 files attached cleanly (`index.css` auto-merged with master's comment edit) and tests grew **813 → 842**, all passing. **We did not touch the unrelated 5 uncommitted items (`.claude/skills/`) in the old working tree** (user instruction).
- **Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 · `npm test` **842** (3 new regression tests — selection indicator `data-selected` · the selection background is not the panel background token · the focus ring 40% value) · ADR lint error 0 · **GUI measurement** = cold-built wt1 on the master base and launched it, compared colors across the three themes (reproduced that the old value is identical to the panel in light · e-ink → confirmed the new value differs in all three themes) + a screenshot comparison of the 4 tab-layout options.
- **★What was not verified or not fixed★:** ① The focus ring 40% is below 3:1 contrast in all three themes and in e-ink is fainter than the always-on border — kept since it is a value the user picked by eye, with the cost recorded in ADR-0168 ② bar↔active tab contrast 1.07:1 — the active decision is carried not by lightness alone but by four things together: text color · separator · `×` ③ in e-ink `--bg` is brighter than `--bg-secondary` so the tab lightness relation is inverted ④ in e-ink the sash accent color and the divider are the same color (`--accent` = `--border` = `#000`) ⑤ `Inter` in `--font-claude-prose` is also not installed but it is inside the slot so out of scope ⑥ **the font still depends on system installation** — rendering identically in every environment needs `@font-face` bundling, and a license check must come first so it is undecided (not rejected, held).
- **Side work — the launcher's vite reuse decision is open.** It looked only at "is port 1420 open" and not at "is it ours", so it reused another worktree's (`engram-dashboard-wt3`) dev server as is. On the first run the app rendered **someone else's checkout source**, and had we not printed the computed style it would have been a spot to misdiagnose as "the change did not take". This time we killed that vite and swapped in ours, but **we did not fix the launcher** — a separate matter.

## S20.18 ran the shell package's 217 unit tests for the first time — the cause of death was a manifest link argument (2026-08-24, `v0.3.0/chore/misc`, autonomous session) · ADR-0174 new · `/review code full` 2 rounds (4 reviewers from two families) · `/qa standard` **PASS** · **185 passed / 32 failed**

- **What was blocked.** The 217 `#[cfg(test)]` in `src-tauri/src/**` have **never once been run**, neither locally nor in CI — the built-in lib test target died at the process load stage with `0xC0000139 STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND`.
  - **Cause.** `tauri-build`/`embed-resource` attach the Windows `RT_MANIFEST` resource with `cargo:rustc-link-arg-bins=`, but Cargo applies it only to `[[bin]]` targets. Without the manifest, comctl32 v5.82 is bound and `TaskDialogIndirect` is missing, and the loader kills the process before `main`.
  - **Proof.** When we injected only the manifest with `mt.exe` into the dying exe, it started up and all 217 ran.
- **The fix has three legs.** `[lib] test = false` (+ `doctest = false`) · a new `[[test]] name = "lib_unit", path = "src/lib.rs"` (kind=test, so the `-tests` link argument reaches it) · `build.rs` finds the resource archive in `$OUT_DIR` and emits `cargo:rustc-link-arg-tests=`. Command = `cargo test -p engram-dashboard --test lib_unit`. The decision and Rejected alternatives are owned by **ADR-0174**.
- **★All 32 failures have one pre-existing cause and are not product defects★** — all are `daemon_client::tests::`, and `start_connection` in `src-tauri/src/daemon_client/mod.rs` returns `Ok(())` without launching the connection task when `app: None`. The test constructors all put in `None`. It has been there since commit `ffcd766` (2026-07-01). Production is always `app: Some` (the only non-test caller is one in `lib.rs`) and the 08-18~08-23 GUI measurements back that up.
- **Two permanent hangs · one stale fixture.** For the two tests that waited forever we put a 5-second `tokio::time::timeout` instead of `#[ignore]`, so `-- --ignored` no longer stops. `prepare_detached_view_empty_slot_is_err` in `layout/manager.rs` was aiming at **a filled slot, not an empty one** — we fixed the fixture and the production guard was right all along.
- **One line added to CI.** `cargo test --locked -p engram-dashboard --test lib_unit -- export_bindings_` (8 tests) — if these eight run it proves all three legs stand, and at the same time it feeds `src-tauri/bindings/` into the existing ts-rs sync gate so that gate now covers **three directories**. ★We deliberately did not register the full suite★ (32 red).
  - Of the 8 `src-tauri/bindings/*.ts`, **5 were actually stale** (e.g. `ViewMeta` was documented as `view:list-updated` while the source says `window:tabs-updated`). We regenerated and committed — only the doc comments changed and the TS type shapes are the same.
- **Documentation cleanup of about 25 files.** The dead `0xC0000139` premise was serving as grounds in about 40 places (workspace `--exclude` · test placement rules · held defects · the description that `src-tauri/bindings/` is maintained by hand). We fixed all of them, and for dated records (step-log · S20 TRD) we did not rewrite but attached **dated correction marks**. We assigned one owner to each fact that goes stale easily — commands and counts to `CLAUDE.md` 「빌드·검증 명령」, the `--lib` pitfall to `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, the cause to `daemon_client/mod.rs`, the reason to ADR-0174, the remaining gap to `docs/tracking.md` T-27.
- **Verification:** `/review code full` 2 rounds (4 reviewers from two families, BLOCK → FIX, all findings applied) · `/qa standard` **PASS** — `cargo build` · workspace regression 1730 passed/0 failed · shell integration 4 targets (49 · 82 · 4 · 9) · `lib_unit` 185/32 (both gate conditions met) · `cargo fmt --check` · 3 isolation gates · `npx tsc --noEmit` · vitest 881 passed. **The two families independently converged on the same two findings** (bounded wait instead of `#[ignore]` · the `libresource.a` branch of `*-pc-windows-gnu`) — both applied.
- **★What was not verified or not fixed★:** ① **We did not touch the 32 failures** — fixing the `app: None` harness is a **user decision** (three shapes: inject a fake `AppHandle` · thread `Option<AppHandle>` through 16 emit points · extract an emitter port trait modeled on the same module's `ViewCommandPort`/`NoViewCommands` — ADR-0012). The ADR for that decision has been pending since 2026-06-30 and has no number yet ② **The 2026-08-23 user decision (discard tests that could not run then) now stands on a dead premise** — 185 of them pass. We did not touch it and only left a mark; only the user can look back on it ③ `--lib` and `--all-targets` still die with `0xC0000139` — `[lib] test = false` only removes it from the **default selection**. We only recorded it and it cannot be closed with the manifest ④ **No GUI measurement this session** (no UI behavior change) ⑤ the `lib_unit` gate criterion has **0 margin** — the cap is 32 and the actual is exactly 32 ⑥ **ADR 0170 remains an empty number** — the `/adr` script numbers only by max+1 and has no means to overwrite, so we could not keep the reservation the previous handoff had written. This decision landed as 0174.

## S20.19 closed the 32 failures with an emitter port, and fixed the 8 silent connection-closing spots it exposed (2026-08-25, `v0.3.0/fix/shell-test-harness`, mixed conversation → autonomous) · `/review code full` 3 rounds (two families) · `/qa` gates **PASS** (no GUI measurement) · **ran the workspace regression without `--exclude` for the first time: 2102 passed / 0 failed**

- **① The 32 failures were a harness defect — not a product defect** (the item S20.18 deferred by user decision). `DaemonClient` holds `app: Option<tauri::AppHandle>` solely for webview emit, but `start_connection` returned `Ok(())` **without launching the connection task** when it was `None`. The test constructors all use `None`, so the socket never opened, the state stuck at `Connecting`, and every `Connected` assertion broke. It had been there since `ffcd766` (2026-07-01) and was invisible until the target ran.
  - **Injecting a fake `AppHandle` is impossible** — what `tauri::test::mock_app()` gives is `AppHandle<MockRuntime>`, not `Wry`, and generalizing over `R: Runtime` spreads to every command signature. So we extracted an **emitter port** — `trait DaemonEvents` + the real adapter `TauriEmitter(AppHandle)` + a no-op `NoDaemonEvents`, held as `Arc<dyn DaemonEvents>`, with the early return deleted. It is modeled on the same module's `ViewCommandPort`/`NoViewCommands` (ADR-0012), and is the third of the three shapes S20.18 put up.
  - ★**Production behavior does not change**★ — the 11 emit spots are all identical in event name · payload shape · order · condition, and the reviewer went down to the frontend listeners to compare. The three contract strings (`connected` · `reconnecting` · `down`) are owned by the `ConnectionStateEvent` enum so a typo does not compile.
- **★② What it exposed is a real product defect, in 8 places★** — paths that take a connection to `Down` while **announcing nothing**. The worst is when the `connect()` caller has vanished after the handshake succeeded — every webview received `connected` and then never got another notice, so **the output channel stays bound to a dead connection** (the frontend's only self-recovery is a pull at refresh time, which does not run on a live page). `close()` has the same hole — the closing window updates only itself and the connection task is already stale and quiet, so **no one notifies the other windows.**
  - We did a **full audit of the 14 production call sites** of `publish_if_current`. **Seven now announce under the generation guard, and two are intentionally silent with the reason written** — one because the connection task already announced the same failure at the same generation so adding it would double-report, and one because it is a `Drop` path and cannot report whether a transition happened and panics are forbidden. Silence without a reason is 0.
- **③ Three things that landed together.**
  - ★The full `lib_unit` suite went onto CI★ and we removed `--exclude engram-dashboard` from the workspace regression (both CI and the local `/qa` list). The two layers guard **different legs** of ADR-0174 — the workspace step is a default-target selection so it catches when `[lib] test = false` is erased, and the named `--test lib_unit` step fails on the spot if the `[[test]]` declaration disappears. **The workspace step structurally cannot see the latter — if the target is erased it is silence, not failure.**
  - The pass criterion for that suite in the `/qa` binding was **「실패 ≤ 32」** — after the fix it is a value that would silently pass up to 32 regressions. We changed it to FAIL unless green, and **forbade writing a total as a threshold**.
  - ★**We corrected one attribution error**★ — what the user actually said on 2026-08-23 was only 「기존 테스트 파일에 미련을 갖지 않는다 — 분리 가능한 단위에 초점을 맞춘다」, but a session rewrote it as "discard 209" and built four conclusions on top of it. The user confirmed they never said such a thing — we withdrew the rewritten sentence and the four derived conclusions and left the original decision as is.
- **Verification:** `/review code full` **3 rounds · two families** (Claude + GPT), all findings applied · `/qa` gates — ran `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=4` **without `--exclude` for the first time**, **42 test binaries · 2102 passed / 0 failed** (the `[[bin]]` test harness was also confirmed to link and start, 0 occurrences of `0xC0000139` in the log — a bin's test harness is still kind Bin so it receives the `-bins` link argument) · `lib_unit` **228 passed / 0 failed** (reproduced 25 times in a row) · shell integration 4 targets green · `cargo fmt --check` · isolation gates · `npx tsc --noEmit` · vitest.
  - We **mutation-verified** all new tests (revert the fix to confirm red → restore). Some rewrote fixed sleeps as `oneshot` gates (ADR-0038), and one flake that got a "dead port" by binding a listener and dropping it was removed.
- **★What was not verified or not fixed★:** ① **Guard→emit is not atomic** — if after `publish_if_current` returns `true` a subsequent `connect()` puts a `connected` on before the emit runs, a late `down` overwrites the latest screen. The structure is the same as the 4 pre-existing spots but **the surface roughly doubled** and `close()` is the most exposed (close→connect is an ordinary user order). The right solution is systemic — an ordered emit queue drained by a single consumer, or carrying a generation marker so the frontend sorts. ★It cannot be solved by emitting while holding the lock★ (ADR-0006). We only recorded it in code and did not implement it ② **There is no deterministic test for removing `close()`'s double `Down` send** — `tokio::watch` bumps a version rather than queueing, so a receiver that did not wake in between cannot distinguish two sends from the same thread. What we pinned is only the primitive contract (`is_current` reports without publishing), and the call-site choice relies on review ③ **The `Arc` cycle keeps the production client alive so `Drop` does not run there** — breaking it with `Weak` was judged out of scope (it requires rewiring the live command path, and a process-lifetime singleton is closer to intended than to a leak). The day it is broken, one of the three reasons `Drop` is silent must be re-decided ④ **No GUI measurement this session** (no UI behavior change · the outgoing event vocabulary is byte-identical) ⑤ **ADR 0170 is still an empty number** — the `/adr` script numbers only by max+1 and has no means to overwrite ⑥ **We reviewed a CI path filter and deliberately did not add it** — even a docs-only push runs the whole 7-minute pipeline. The cost is 0 (public repository), but turning the filter on makes "there is no run for this SHA" a normal state and leaves the open matter of rewording the merge convention that demands per-commit green to match.

## Next (not started)

- **[✅ Decision made 2026-08-14 — ADR-0158] A version mismatch is announced, not cut off.** The direction item below is closed by this ADR. Decision = the protocol version is not raised (the bump criterion narrowed to 「봉투 문법이 깨질 때」) · check the peer's capabilities before sending (the daemon advertises first right after connecting, so nothing unknown is ever sent to an old daemon — confirmed by measurement) · no automatic daemon shutdown · **notice = once at app start, announce only, a small trace once dismissed** (no action button, a modal only when it cannot attach at all) · independent of version, a deadline and an error correlation display are laid down together. Rationale research = `docs/research/daemon-version-mismatch-2026-08-14.md` (adversarial review BLOCK → recommendation corrected, and that history is in that document too).
- **[Long-term direction logged 2026-08-14 — found in the research] Generation overlap + letting the old generation wither.** Start the new daemon in a separate place and send only new connections to it, and **leave the old daemon as it is until the sessions it holds finish.** This is the standard technique of the proxy-server family and the only way to solve 「데몬을 죽이면 안 된다」 (a user principle) **structurally**. Not in scope now — the first candidate when daemon lifetime · upgrade is looked at again.
- **[Old item — closed by ADR-0158 above] Be tolerant quietly, announce when the impact is large.** The tolerance side of ADR-0157 (unknown fields in hop-to-hop wiring are ignored and executed with the old meaning) is **correct to stay quiet in normal times** — popping up every time one more field arrives is noise. **But when that version difference has a major impact on the system, it must be announced once with a popup** (user direction). This is not a new task but **the same place as an already logged gap** — the record (the phase4 non-blocking gate earlier in this file) that at the `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1→2 bump a 「새 셸 + 살아 있는 옛 데몬」 falls into endless 'reconnecting' with `VersionMismatch` and the user cannot see the reason. To look at together when starting = 「무엇을 지대한 영향으로 판정하나」 (a protocol version mismatch is certain · ignoring unknown fields is not) and the notice surface (the terminal 'down' state + guidance).
- **[Open — must be decided when a remote frontend attaches] Is a remote · mobile connector 「우리 프로그램」 or 「입구」?** ADR-0157 separates layers by origin, and that decision rests on **the premise that the party is our own deliverable** (three: daemon · shell · webview). When a remote frontend or a third-party client attaches, that premise breaks — if it is ours, tolerance; if someone else's, treat it as an entrance and rejection is right. Right now there is no such connector, so exposure is 0, but **the moment one attaches, drifting toward tolerance without a decision means quietly ignoring unknown fields sent by someone else.**

**[S20 trace-discard review logged 2026-08-17 — caught by `/review code deep` with 3 reviewers (doc-aware breaker · cross-family blind · concurrency/lifetime lens) and deferred by the user.]**

- **★(ra) After a handover, if the *taking-over side* disconnects, the previous owner's **live** name vanishes permanently — ★user decision 2026-08-17: deferred to slice B. But it is closed before slice B starts★** (all three reviewers found the same sequence and only the severity differed — blind HIGH/security · doc-aware MED/regression · concurrency LOW. By convention the main agent cannot decide, so the user ruled).
  - Sequence: A connects · registers → B connects · registers the same name (`Roster::register` **permits the handover as legitimate** — TRD §3-7 clause 1) → B disconnects → `remove_owner(B)` deletes that name → A is alive and implements that command, but **registration happens once on attach**, so there is no occasion to raise it again. Result = `UNKNOWN_COMMAND` + `retry: never` + vanishing from the lookup. In the trace era it stayed as `available:false`, so the name · shape were visible and it had `retry: after-condition`.
  - **★Caution against confusion — this session actually got confused once★:** the overlap 「A가 끊기는 도중에 B가 붙는」 is **safe.** `disconnect` takes down only the names it still owns, so B's registration is protected (`roster.rs:294-295`). The dangerous one is where **A stays alive to the end.**
  - **★Why a one-line fix (「남이 쥐고 있으면 거절」) does not work★:** the daemon does not notice a half-open connection for up to **50 seconds** (`DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `net/src/ws.rs:53`). If the shell reconnects in that window and declares its own name, **it looks held by its own corpse and is rejected.** The value that tells 「같은 클라가 되찾는 것」 from 「남이 빼앗는 것」 is **not in the connection identity** — that value is exactly slice B's client-made identifier. So the moment this defect becomes real and the moment the distinguishing means arrives are **in the same place**, and putting in a half rule now would mean tearing it up again then.
  - **Unreachable today — and the reason is stronger than 「셸이 연결 하나만 연다」: there are 0 pieces of code that *send* a registration** (daemon · shell · frontend, all of them. Every reference that shows up is inside `#[cfg(test)]` — measured 2026-08-17). Only the receiving side stands.
  - **★An alternative the user raised (to look at together during slice B): store the *previous owner* for each name too, and when the taking-over side disconnects, revert to the previous owner★** — this is exactly the place that ADR-0150 alternative G (「이름 하나에 주인 여럿」 deferred) points at. **What must be answered together when reviving it = does that list not grow without bound?** Piling up dead owners per name is **on the same axis** as the trace that was just discarded (the one ADR-0150 Decision 3 closed).
- **(ma) The disconnect-handling unit (owner token) and the live-roster unit (connection id) are out of step — another face of the same landmine as (ra), so deferred together.** Today it is harmless because `owner_of` is 1:1 with the connection. The moment slice B takes the identifier out of the connection, `detach(conn1)` erases **even the registrations of a live connection using the same identifier**, and that connection keeps passing `refuse_if_detached`, so **it does not know it was erased** (registration happens once on attach). `command_roster.rs:83-87` vs `:134-139`. **To fix it now, the removal unit would have to be narrowed to the connection, but `ConnId` is a type the tool crate does not know, so the act of fixing itself pre-decides slice B's owner model.** So this time only a load-bearing comment was left in the code.
- **[✅ Decision made 2026-08-18 — S20.11] (ba) The recorded premise has no force — 「등록 패킷의 원소 개수 상한은 `net`의 프레임 크기 제한이 질 몫이다」 (last line of Step 1 log (n) below).** `WebSocketConfig` is not configured anywhere in the repository, so the tungstenite 0.26.2 **defaults** apply — **64 MiB** per message · **16 MiB** per frame (measured: vendor source `tungstenite-0.26.2/src/protocol/mod.rs:101-102`). Duplicate names bypass the count check of `check_room_for` (it counts **after** deduplication), and the length check · insertion loop walks the full amount. `update`'s `removed` has **no count cap at all**. **This change did not create it** (that code is unchanged) · only an authenticated loopback peer can reach it. **A separate matter.** **Decision = no cap is set** (user decision 2026-08-18) — what reaches it is only an authenticated local peer, and to fix a cap value, how many items the screen actually declares has to be settled first. History = S20.11 above.
- **[✅ Decision made 2026-08-18 — S20.11] (sa) The notification surface for retry degradation is 0 — an unrecorded consequence of the loss ADR-0150 accepted.** Merging the two errors was a decision, but as a result the `retry: never` the caller gets goes out for **a name that comes back up to 50 seconds later**, and since there is no push to announce roster changes (`CommandList` is request-response only), the caller has **no occasion to rediscover**. The accepted wording extends only to 「두 오류의 구분 포기」, and 「통지 없는 종결적 포기」 is outside it. **A separate matter.** **Decision = no notification surface is created** (user decision 2026-08-18) — 「다시 치지 마라」 is enough, and if the problem is actually observed it will be handled then. **★Condition to revisit — the way of lowering the retry instruction is blocked by ADR-0150's abandonment of the distinction★:** applying the 「안전 × 쓸모」 yardstick of ADR-0159, set down today, to this place gives the 「다시 물어봐라」 side, but because ADR-0150 gave up the distinction between 「끊긴 이름」 and 「없는 이름」, lowering it that way makes **even a nonexistent name typed by mistake get the same answer, causing endless retries** — it cannot be lowered unless that distinction is revived. History = S20.11 above.

**[S20 Step 2 slice 3 log 2026-08-16 — unified command bus] What was deferred rather than fixed while replacing the wall. The 「S20 Step 1 리뷰 적립」 block right below remains open as is — not written again here.**

- **★(ga) The rejection message returns the caller's string without a length limit — a cap was added and then reverted, and that revert is intended★.** This is not a defect this slice created (the old door at HEAD had it too and `/control/send` still has it). **What breaks before reviving it:** one fix round put a 4096-byte cap on `ControlQueryResult::to_json`, but for the agent family the contract is that the hint attaches a recovery command that can be typed at the **tail**, so cutting the tail removes that command entirely. Measured = `POST /control/agent {"verb":"spawn","target":"a"×5000}` → hint 5182 B → wire 4122 B, **0 backticks**. The caller gets back the 4 KB it sent and does not get the next step. **User decision: revert the cap entirely, and open the length limit as a separate task with its own decision record.**
  - **Leaking places (so that task does not search again):** `unknown_verb` (`crates/engram-dashboard-daemon/src/control/agent.rs`) · the `reason` of `malformed_body` (same file — if the body is a JSON **string**, the serde message carries the entire body. `preview` shortens only `raw` and does not shorten `reason`) · the token echo in the core's target-missing · conflict · exhausted messages (`crates/engram-dashboard-core/src/agent/commands.rs`) · `SendReject::GroupNotFound` of `/control/send` (`crates/engram-dashboard-daemon/src/control/ingress.rs`) — **this has a different envelope type** (`ControlResult::to_json`), so that cap never covered it in the first place (reachable with `{"to":["@"+"x"×900000]}`).
  - **Reach conditions (for judging size):** 127.0.0.1 only · credential gate · 1 MiB body cap · the production caller is the `engram` CLI alone (it does not limit the length of the values it forwards and prints the daemon response as is).
  - **★Do not write the sentence 「여기가 유일한 상한 지점」★** — it was written that way four rounds in a row and was false all four times. That pattern is the reason this axis was taken out of the slice's scope.
- **(na) 3 net holes the review recorded (not fixed):**
  - **Nobody checks whether the recovery command survives to the wire in a long hint.** `every_rejection_carries_the_typed_code_and_a_runnable_command` (`crates/engram-dashboard-daemon/src/control/agent.rs`) looks at the result enum **before** serialization, and every integration test that serializes uses short messages. Even if the cap comes back, there is no test that would catch the loss of the tail.
  - **`move`'s reply is not a snapshot at one point in time** — the name is read **after** the parent is changed, `parent` is the value this call put in, and an agent that disappears right after being moved also gets `Ok`. It is written in a code comment and **intentionally not changed.**
  - **The required/optional dichotomy of `agent.spawn` cannot hold an XOR** (`target` vs `cwd` mutually exclusive). The per-field guidance is right, but the combination constraint is not in the model.

**[User direction 2026-08-12 — unified command bus: the work of raising ADR-0022 from proposed to confirmed] Humans and LLMs assemble and fire the same commands, the branch is only up to "who assembles", and after that they merge. There is one command.** This is a layout the user derived in conversation, and it **points at the same place as ADR-0022 (proposed, only the direction fixed on 2026-06-17)** — shaping the form of that "later" is what this item does.
- **Core form:** declare command names · arguments in **one place in Rust** and **auto-generate** the TypeScript side. It is not a new scheme — the wire definitions already run that way (23 generated files) and a gate catches any drift. It applies that machinery once more to the command vocabulary.
- **★Owner designation is unnecessary — the definition location is the owner (corrected by the user's remark)★:** the main agent first proposed "put an owner field on each command", but if each module declares its own commands, **the declaration site is itself the declaration** so the field is redundant. However, **screen-only commands** (theme · chat appearance) have no Rust module and drop out of the list, so **only the declaration is given a place in Rust** (declaration and implementation are separated like a C++ header — `theme.set` exists in Rust as a name only, and the code that does the work is in TypeScript).
- **The executor cannot be shared — only the contract is shared:** there are three owners (daemon = agents · mail / thin app wrapper = windows · tabs · slots / screen = theme · chat) and **all are different processes**, so the functions themselves cannot be gathered. Each registers its own handler, and **"if a name is generated but there is no handler, fail loudly"** is enforced (the menu already does this — an unregistered `commandId` drops the item and logs an error).
- **Structure name = ports and adapters (the user pointed it out).** The command list = port contract · menu / command line = incoming adapter · each module's handler = core. This is vocabulary this project already uses (messaging kernel = port-owning structure, ADR-0110). **One difference = here the port crosses processes** → a propagation device (relay) is needed in a real form.
- **★Prerequisite = implement the relay (ADR-0081). Without it, even if the lists are merged, the agent cannot call screen-side commands★** — and that is already pinned as follow-up order ② of ADR-0132 Decision 7. **That is, the user's layout and the existing roadmap point at the same place.**
- **Current state (measured):** inside the screen, human clicks · shortcuts · the LLM already take **the same entrance** (a menu item carries a `commandId` and resolves title · execution from the registry). Three things are out of step — ① only the LLM has **two side doors** (`__engramLayout`·`__engramChat`) (the layout one admits in its own comment that it is "a temporary path until the formal command bus" · "a parallel path") ② the screen vocabulary (`agent.spawn`) and the daemon vocabulary (`spawn`, `CLI_AGENT_VERBS` — `core/src/agent/types.rs`) **do not know each other** (the verb composition actually differs too) ③ the agent has no way to know the names of screen-only commands.
- **Unresolved forks (research targets):** ① generation scope = names only or **down to the argument shape**? (main's recommendation = down to arguments — it is the method verified on the wire, and with names only, the problem of the vocabularies splitting today would repeat at the argument layer) ② **is a query also a command?** (`__engramChat` mixes in functions that read values, so how to fit them into an "execute"-centred list is undecided) ③ which crate to put the declaration of screen-only commands in — the thin app wrapper is natural but **the daemon does not know the wrapper** (intended design), so **who merges the list and shows it to the agent** remains ④ unconfirmed whether a command can span several owners.
- **How to start:** per this project's convention, **no guessing → `/research` into mature OSS precedents (editor command palette family) → options · trade-offs to the user → update ADR-0022 to confirmed (or a follow-up ADR)**. It is a weighty decision, so the main agent does not settle it arbitrarily.

**[User direction 2026-08-11 — the center of gravity of agent creation · spawn] For spawn, "wake-up" is the main use, and "launching a new one" only needs to exist once for demos.** The real-use flow is ① the user creates agents in advance ② when needed, **wake a sleeping one and hand it work** (e.g. if a QA · review agent is in the registry, wake it). A spawn that is given one path and creates an agent on the spot is **for tests · demos**, so no kind-selection option was attached either (piece ②, 2026-08-11). **A much later direction:** the agent **assembles guidelines · skills and so on by itself to make a preset** and spawns with it — at that point the spawn surface will accept **preset assembly** rather than "one path", so do not read today's thin spawn arguments as "unfinished" and extend them. The direction of the extension is different.
- **[User direction 2026-08-04 — to look at together in the agent control system chapter] Control plane = CLI + discovery instead of enumeration** — mail goes through MCP, and **other control (agent spawn · add · delete, UI control, etc.) goes through the CLI** (low frequency, and no separate connection is needed). The key is **not writing the feature list into the priming one by one**: MCP exposes its tool list · schema by itself so one line "look it up there" is enough, and the CLI is also made discoverable via help. The user's sketch = **group help** (grouped into families such as `help agent` · UI control, so one gets back roughly function usage like MCP and handles it). **Not designed deeply now (user instruction)** — it is a place that will be looked at again anyway while building the agent control system, and tangling it up now would make adding to it harder then. The prerequisite decision that opens together = ADR-0086 least-privilege ("who is given control authority"). **1 constraint discovered in advance (must be looked at then):** `engram-send` is a **sibling binary in the same crate** as the daemon, so it comes out in the same directory, and the daemon attaches its **parent directory** to the agent PATH — if the control CLI is also placed as a sibling and attached to PATH the same way, **the mail CLI comes back to life under a bare name** (PATH is permission per directory, not per file). 3 workarounds = ① place the control CLI in a different directory ② give up the bare name and call by absolute path (no PATH injection — a parallel wiring like `ENGRAM_SEND_EXE` is already a precedent) ③ merge into one binary with subcommands and lock the mail verbs according to capability.

Therefore ① the MCP branch does **not strip** the credentials · PATH the profile put in ② **no warning** is added for that state either. Narrow the ADR-0128 invariant sentence to this scope (the whole environment → the daemon's provisioning act).

- **[✅ Done 2026-08-17] Branch strategy refinement — branch unit = one topic confirmed · commit step prefix · tags for versions only** — **User decision:** reconfirm the branch unit from "a unit of work" to **one topic** (do not cut a new branch per sub-topic; stack all steps · sub-topics of that topic on one branch). Add a **step number prefix** to the commit title (`S21: <타입>(<범위>): <요약>`). Tags are limited to **versions only** (`v1.2.0`) — introducing step tags was considered and rejected. **Rationale:** the research (`/research` medium — peer survey · merge method comparison · 3-way worktree review + external-model adversarial review) found **no industry standard for the branch unit** — the practical literature all presumes teams, so there is no evidence covering the one-person + GUI (Fork) readability condition. So it was decided directly to fit our conditions (2 worktrees in parallel, a workflow of filtering by branch in Fork). **Why step tags were rejected:** a tag is a point, so it cannot do a range filter such as "show only this worktree's work" — the branch does that. Tags are already used by releases (`v*`), so the meanings would mix. **2 things the research corrected (removed from the CLAUDE.md text):** ① the branch name left in a merge commit is free text and not trustworthy metadata — what actually remains is only the parent-child **boundary**. ② `git revert -m 1` is not a means to safely revert a whole chunk — the reverted ancestor does not come back in on later merges. **Deleting `docs/reference/branch-strategy.md`:** the user judged that a discard stamp alone leaves the risk that the next session follows it — the content is preserved in git history, and the current canonical source is unified to `### 브랜치·커밋` of CLAUDE.md 「구현 실행 규약」.

  - ★**The review saved this round — the first implementation was a thing that never catches**★. A Windows spawn passes through one layer of `cmd.exe /c codex …`, so the PID the link gives is the **wrapper** and what holds the lock is the `codex.exe` beneath it. Comparing only the wrapper PID **never produces a match, with no error or log.** All gates were green — **there were 0 tests measuring the wiring** (the deleted status line test was exactly that place) and the matcher fixture planted the holder as 「자식 자신의 pid」 so 14 stayed green even under the defect.   - **So this time a mutation check was hung on every rule** — reverting to wrapper-PID-only comparison made the real-process wiring test FAILED · reverting the three of birth order / visited key / holder counting made the 4 named ones FAILED · reverting the recovery gate to `is_some()` made 2 FAILED. All restored and re-confirmed green.
  - ★**Decision rule — failing to receive is better than receiving wrongly**★: the PID and the **process start time** must both match to be a candidate · **a descendant cannot be born before its parent** (blocks another's orphaned codex from entering via a reused ppid) · the visited mark is `(pid, 시작시각)` · what is counted is not files but **matching holders** · file names only **canonical uuid** · if there are two or more candidates **only that lap is refused** and polling continues · it runs **only on a fresh incarnation** · waiting is polling, not a time window (until it catches or the child dies, the wait doubling from 0.5 seconds up to a 15-second cap).
  - **The trap of `codex resume` was also blocked** — if given a value that cannot be read as a thread id, codex **reinterprets it as a session name**, quietly creates a new session, ends with **exit code 0**, and the turn is billed (measured). If it is a handle that cannot be loaded, the subcommand itself is not emitted. ★Not merged with claude★ — its `--resume` honestly fails on an unknown value (an existing measurement).
